item.title: [Yahoo Sports] How Can Dodgers Legally Get Josue De Paula On Postseason Roster?

item.content:encoded:
In an unprecedented move in the Andrew Friedman era, the Los Angeles Dodgers called up a position player directly from Double-A earlier this month: Josue De Paula.
De Paula is not a good defender, but his bat is off the charts. He has a great eye at the plate and dominated in Double-A. Still, the big leagues are a whole different thing. That has not seemed to bother De Paula, who has a 1.081 OPS in 11 games with 11 walks and just five strikeouts.
De Paula has gotten to serve as the designated hitter with Shohei Ohtani out, but that's about to change. His defense is not good enough to start in left field, and the Dodgers are not going to start him over Andy Pages, Teoscar Hernández or Kyle Tucker right now. However, he would still be a very valuable bat for the postseason, with the ability to get on base at a high clip.
There's one big problem, however. He was not on the 40-man roster on Sept. 1, which is the eligibility cutoff for the postseason. The Dodgers can still legally get De Paula on a postseason roster, but will need to petition the commissioner's office.
"A player who doesn't meet said criteria for postseason eligibility can still be added to a team's roster in the postseason via petition to the Commissioner's Office if the player was in the organization on Aug. 31 and is replacing someone who is on the injured list and has served the minimum amount of time required for activation," read Major League Baseball's rules for postseason eligibility. "(For example, a player on the 10-day injured list who has been on it for at least 10 days, or a player who has been on the 60-day injured list for at least 60 days.) Players who are acquired in September or after are ineligible."
De Paula is good on the first need, but the Dodgers would have to say he's replacing Dalton Rushing, who is the only current Dodger who has exceeded a minimum stay on the injured list. This would make sense, as Rushing may not be able to catch anyway and would be used as a pinch hitter. De Paula can fill that role.
More MLB: Dodgers' Freddie Freeman Explains Why Dodgers Need Bye This Year

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

23 Sep 2026, 19:49 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Jayne Kamin)
Shohei Ohtani is expected to be back in the starting lineup Wednesday, Yoshinobu Yamamoto will be on the mound and the Los Angeles Dodgers will accelerate their playoff preparations in a home game against the San Diego Padres.
Ohtani last played Sept. 7, one day after he struck out a season-high four times, and has been on the injured list with right biceps discomfort ever since.
With five regular-season games remaining, Ohtani will get a chance to build some momentum for the postseason.
'Unless I hear otherwise, he'll be in the lineup,' said Dodgers manager Dave Roberts, who admitted that the team's leading home-run hitter with 30 is about an '8 or 9' on a health scale of 1-10.
Where to put Ohtani in the lineup is another question. Normally the Dodgers' leadoff hitter, Mookie Betts has made the top spot his own lately.
With the Padres set to start left-hander Robbie Ray, the right-handed Betts likely is to hit leadoff Wednesday, while Ohtani could be in his former No. 2 spot. Betts went 1-for-4 with an RBI and a run scored in Tuesday's 7-0 victory over the Padres and is batting .366 since the start of September.
Yamamoto (14-8, 2.51 ERA) has looked like an ace all season and has been at his best of late by going 3-1 with a 1.79 ERA over his last seven starts. The right-hander is 3-3 with a 3.76 ERA in seven career starts against San Diego.
The Dodgers (97-60) increased their home winning streak to 11 games and reduced their magic number to two for clinching a bye through the wild-card round. They also pulled within a game of the National League-leading Milwaukee Brewers (98-59).
Los Angeles center fielder Andy Pages returned from a broken hand on Tuesday and reached base twice.
'Obviously being out for a month, I'm not feeling all that great or familiar at the plate but there are things from the Trajekt (pitching machine) that helped me come back,' Pages said through a team interpreter.
The Padres' magic number for clinching a wild-card spot remained at two after Tuesday's loss.
Ray (13-8, 3.60) pitched well immediately after he was acquired from the San Francisco Giants at the trade deadline but has an 8.78 ERA over his past three starts. He is 3-2 with a 5.22 ERA in eight starts for San Diego.
In 26 career starts against the Dodgers, tied for his most against any club, Ray is 9-9 with a 3.81 ERA.
The Padres (87-70) entered Tuesday's series opener against the Dodgers with 13 victories in their previous 14 games but failed to find much offense as Los Angeles went to a bullpen game and used eight pitchers.
It was the second time since the All-Star break the Padres were held without a run.
San Diego also is expected to activate right-hander Jason Adam following a shoulder injury as he rejoins one of the major league's best bullpens. Adam is 2-2 with a 2.51 ERA in 36 relief appearances but has not pitched in a big-league game since June 29.
'Yeah, more than ready,' Adam said, according to the San Diego Union-Tribune. 'I feel 100% ready.'
Padres manager Craig Stammen was guarded with the team's plans.
'It's good to see him back pitching in his normal way,' Stammen said. 'Hopefully we'll have him activated before the season ends.'
--Field Level Media

I’m just happy I got hits w
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA — Freddie Freeman delivered three RBI in the Dodgers’ 7-0 win over the Padres on Tuesday night, continuing his recent rebound at the plate. After struggling through much of September, the veteran first baseman appears to be finding his stroke just as the postseason approaches. Following the game, Freeman talked about his recent improvement, the Dodgers’ increasingly healthy lineup and the importance of securing a first-round bye.
“It’s a little better. I’m just happy I got hits when I needed to get hits. Today and the last couple of games have been a lot better, so hopefully we’re trending in the right direction when we need to.”
Freeman is also encouraged by what he’s seeing from the rest of the lineup, particularly with Andy Pages back from his hand injury and Shohei Ohtani expected to return Wednesday.
“It’s been really good. You’ve got guys swinging the bat who got off to tough starts. Kyle’s been great. Teo’s been hot. Guys are starting to come back that we’ve been missing over the last couple of weeks, too. It’s good to see Andy back, and Sho coming back tomorrow. A lot of good things happening for the offense lately.”
With the Dodgers’ magic number for clinching the National League’s second seed down to one, Freeman has his sights set on getting that job done.
“I feel like we’ve just been playing really good baseball as a group lately as well. We had to step up when guys went down, and that’s a credit to the guys that have been going. You want to be playing well going into the playoffs. We need one more win for that bye. That’s what we need. We need that, get some rest, and then have a great week of practicing going into the playoffs. Guys are swinging the bats at the right time, and hopefully we can carry that.”
Asked why the first-round bye is particularly important for this year’s club, Freeman laughed.
“I think we all know why it’s important. There’s a lot of us kind of limping toward the end here. A lot of aches and pains this year. It’s good to get those guys back on the field and get some at-bats in them, then rest up and get some more at-bats during the live sessions and whatever we do during that week to get us ready for Saturday.”
More Dodgers Coverage:
Have you subscribed to the Bleed Los Podcast YouTube channel? Be sure to ring the notification bell to watch player interviews, participate in shows & promotions, and stay up to date on all Dodgers news and rumors!
A lifelong baseball fan, Webb has been going to Dodger games since he moved to Los Angeles in 1987. His favorite memory was attending the insane Game 3 of the World Series in 2025 and hugging random Dodgers fans after Freddie’s walkoff homer. He has been writing for Dodgersbeat since 2020.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers' Freddie Freeman Explains Why Dodgers Need Bye This Year
item.dc:creator: Aaliyan Mohammed
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers won the World Series in 2024 with a first-round bye, and won it last year as the Nol. 3 seed, having to play in a Wild Card Series. They've shown they can win both ways, but a bye this year is a little more important. The Dodgers stars are only getting older, and with age comes wear and tear. The team has been pretty banged up, and it's no secret that they want the extra rest. "I think we all know why it's important," first baseman Freddie Freeman said, per Sporting Tribu
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers won the World Series in 2024 with a first-round bye, and won it last year as the Nol. 3 seed, having to play in a Wild Card Series.
They've shown they can win both ways, but a bye this year is a little more important. The Dodgers stars are only getting older, and with age comes wear and tear. The team has been pretty banged up, and it's no secret that they want the extra rest.
"I think we all know why it's important," first baseman Freddie Freeman said, per Sporting Tribune's Fredo Cervantes. "There's a lot of us kind of limping toward the end here. A lot of aches and pains this year."
Freeman is not kidding when he talks about the Dodgers "limping" to the finish line, even though he said it while chuckling. Shohei Ohtani is currently on the injured list, Freeman is playing through some knee issues, Andy Pages just got back in the lineup after a fractured hand and Blake Snell exited his last start after just one inning.
Not to mention the normal wear and tear a 162-game season takes on players. The Dodgers have the oldest lineup in baseball, and they could use a bye more than anyone. Not getting the bye would mean a date with either San Diego, Chicago, Philadelphia or Arizona in a best-of-three series.
Any of those matchups would be much tougher than the matchup the Dodgers had against the Cincinnati Reds in the Wild Card last year. Any one of those teams could upset the Dodgers in a Wild Card Series. However, it's hard to imagine a team coming out of a tough Wild Card Series and beating a rested Dodgers squad with its pitching lined up.

item.title: [Just Baseball] The Dodgers' Max Muncy Continues To Be Underrated | Just Baseball
item.dc:creator: Clay Snowden

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles, California. The city of movie stars, names and big personalities. Oh yeah, and championships, with the two most recent going to the Dodgers. When you think about the Los Angeles Dodgers, the names that come to mind are Shohei, Tarik, Yoshinobu, and Mookie.
Not Max.
For one reason or another, Max Muncy has been an underappreciated player in this league for far too long. No, he’s not the typical profile to win an MVP; he doesn’t have the flair that matches the city, and maybe consistency just isn’t sexy.
But, remove Max Muncy from the Los Angeles Dodgers, and this season, along with their recent history, looks different.
Stats from prior to games on Sept. 20, 2026.
Muncy’s Importance in 2026
Although the Dodgers easily clinched another NL West title, I think it’s fair to say their season has not gone quite as planned. Crazy, right? When you have their amount of star power and top prospects, and you acquire Tarik Skubal at the deadline, anything less than the best record in baseball isn’t good enough.
Part of the reason why the Dodgers have not reached the extremely high expectations many placed on them is injuries. Shohei Ohtani, Will Smith, Roki Sasaki, Andy Pages, Dalton Rushing, Edwin Díaz, Tyler Glasnow, Blake Snell, and others all missed significant time on the IL.
Combine that IL time with Kyle Tucker’s ho-hum season and Mookie Betts not being quite the player he once was at the plate, and you can see why the Dodgers don’t quite look like an unstoppable force.
With so many injuries and inconsistencies in the lineup, the Dodgers needed Max Muncy more than ever. Even at 36 years old, Muncy is having an amazing season. He is slashing .254/.351/.500 with 29 home runs and a 132 wRC+, second on the team only to Ohtani’s 142 wRC+. Muncy’s 4.3 fWAR is first amongst Dodgers position players. Yes, that includes Ohtani.
He’s currently on pace to either match or surpass his career high of 4.5 fWAR from the 2021 season when he hit 36 home runs. If he doesn’t quite get to 4.5, 4.4 would tie his second-best season, which came in 2019 in the juiced-ball era. Yeah, I’d say Muncy’s doing pretty well.
After being such a consistent and healthy player throughout the beginning part of his career, Muncy missed parts of the last two seasons due to injury. Returning from injury to play over 140 games, and at this high of a level, goes to show what type of talent he is.
On the current roster, Muncy is one of three players with more than 20 home runs. Keep in mind, Ohtani also has more than 20, but he is on the IL. Muncy’s 29 home runs place him in the top 20 in all of baseball. We still saw his power in his injury-riddled seasons in 2024 and 2025, but seeing it return to this level has been a massive boost for the Dodgers.
Kyle Tucker was seen as a middle-of-the-order bat who could push Muncy down a spot, but as it has turned out, Muncy is more important than ever. Sure, this team would still have topped 90 wins without Muncy, but the lineup would feel much different. The hole created at third base would be filled by Miguel Rojas or Enrique Hernández, which is far from ideal. The drop-off from Muncy to whoever the replacement was would have been massive.
As you look ahead to the postseason, there are still questions around the Dodgers’ lineup. Pages recently returned from the IL, and Ohtani will soon, giving the Dodgers a much-needed boost. Pages adds another righty bat into the lineup and allows Tommy Edman to move back to the infield. Ohtani fills DH, which is currently held down by rookie Josue De Paula.
Muncy adds another veteran back with postseason experience. A .817 OPS and 16 career postseason home runs give the Dodgers another threat once the weather cools and the games become more important.
Yes, Muncy has been crucial to the Dodgers’ success this season. But you could really say that about his entire career.
Muncy’s Consistent Excellence
Let’s start back at the beginning. Max Muncy started with the Oakland Athletics before being released in 2017 and signing a minor league contract with the Dodgers. He debuted in LA in 2018, immediately finding success, slashing .263/.391/.582 with 35 home runs. From an Oakland castoff to hitting 35 home runs a year later was impressive, but it was just the beginning.
Muncy followed in 2019, repeating his 35-home run season, a mark he has posted four times since joining the Dodgers. Power has been an important part of his game, and so has consistency. From 2018 through 2023, Muncy logged at least 135 games each year, excluding the COVID season.
Of those six seasons, three were at 130 wRC+ or better, and five were over 100. Really, the only subpar season of his career came in 2020, when he had a 98 wRC+ and 12 home runs in 58 games.
His 2024 and 2025 shortened seasons were still, statistically, some of the best of his career. If we look at it just from a wRC+ standpoint, his 133 wRC+ in 2024 and 137 in 2025 rank in the top four in his career, while 2026 (132 wRC+) lands in the same discussion.
By now, you know what you’re getting with Muncy. Consistent power and one of the best walk rates in the league. His batting average isn’t going to wow anyone, and neither is his defense, although both are adequate in this day and age.
Max Muncy is one of the best Dodgers of all time, and you might not even realize it. His 238 career home runs rank fifth in Dodger history. He ranks seventh in walks, roughly 100 behind Jackie Robinson. Only 14 Dodgers have driven in more runs, and by the time Muncy hangs up the cleats, he could be near the top 10.
Year in and year out, Muncy gives the Dodgers exactly what they expect of him. Early in his career, he provided versatility around the diamond. If the team needed a second baseman, he’d play there. When they needed a first baseman in 2021, Muncy was the answer. Now, he’s settled into third base.
Three All-Star appearances and three World Series rings. I’d argue that he deserves more recognition. Not too bad for a guy that they got for next to nothing.
Final Thoughts
I know that the Dodgers have the type of star power that drives jersey sales. Who wouldn’t want to wear an Ohtani jersey? He’s the best player to ever play the game.
However, I wish we would see more Muncy jerseys at Dodger Stadium. In some ways, this might be a “you don’t know what you’ve got till it’s gone” situation. Luckily, I think Muncy still has several more productive seasons left. He’s not showing signs of slowing down.
If you placed Max Muncy into a number of other cities, he would be their star. I guess it’s easy to get lost in Hollywood, which has over 2,800 of them.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers dismantled the San Diego Padres 7-0 on Tuesday night at Dodger Stadium. Freddie Freeman led the charge, going 2-for-4 with three RBIs in an offense that produced nine hits and four walks against one of the best pitching staffs in the National League.
The Dodgers are 97-60. Their magic number to clinch a first-round playoff bye is one. A win over the Padres on Wednesday or an Atlanta Braves loss to the Reds gets them there.
For most teams, a bye is a nice bonus. For these Dodgers, Freeman made clear it is something far more necessary than that.
Freeman’s Candid Assessment
Freeman was asked after Tuesday’s win why securing the bye matters so much to this team.
“I think we all know why it’s important,” Freeman said. “There’s a lot of us kind of limping toward the end here. A lot of aches and pains this year.”
The Dodgers have dealt with injuries at nearly every position this season. Shohei Ohtani just spent two weeks on the injured list with knee, biceps, and neck issues. Andy Pages missed a month with a fractured hand. Blake Snell has been building back from his own absence. Tyler Glasnow has never made it through a full regular season without an injury since joining the organization.
What the Bye Provides
The Dodgers have won the World Series in each of the last two seasons. They know how October works. They also know what happens when a team enters the postseason at less than full strength.
A first-round bye would give the Dodgers nearly a week off before the Division Series. It allows pitchers to reset their arms. It allows hitters coming off the injured list, Ohtani and Pages, to get additional at-bats in intrasquad games rather than jumping straight into a high-leverage series.
Freeman’s three-RBI performance on Tuesday was a reminder that the lineup is dangerous when everyone is healthy and clicking. Will Smith and Tommy Edman each homered. Mookie Betts added an RBI double. Kyle Tucker picked up a hit. The pieces are there. The question is whether they can stay on the field long enough to use them.
“We’re playing good baseball,” Freeman said. “We need to carry it on for the next five games.”
Final Word for the Dodgers
The Dodgers are built to win another championship. The talent is there. The pitching is there. The experience is there. What they need now is time. Time to heal. Time to reset. And time to arrive at the postseason as close to full strength as possible.
One more win and the bye is theirs. Freeman made the case for why nothing matters more right now.

item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers received two key reinforcements making their returns from injury on Tuesday, as both Andy Pages and Roki Sasaki played a factor into the team’s 7-0 shutout win over the San Diego Padres.
The Dodgers are preparing to get the final Infinity Stone added to their gauntlet, as two-way superstar Shohei Ohtani is expected to return from the injured list for Wednesday’s game against San Diego. Whether Ohtani will remain in the leadoff spot in the starting lineup is still up in the air, as Mookie Betts has been swinging a red-hot bat at the leadoff spot in his absence, per Sonja Chen of MLB.com.
“I do think I should think through the Mookie vs. left situation, but I have to think about the entire lineup structure,” Roberts said. “That’s probably the way it’s going to fall out, but I haven’t totally decided yet.”
Roki Sasaki made his first bullpen appearance since the 2025 World Series on Tuesday, as he logged a scoreless top of the fourth inning while allowing just one hit and striking out two.
Although Sasaki has vastly improved in the second half this season before suffering a blister to his pitching hand— 5.33 ERA in first half, 2.97 ERA in second half— the plan is to once again have him out of the bullpen for the postseason for a second consecutive year, per Chen.
“It’s just showing that whatever it takes to help us win, knowing that any inning he throws in the postseason is going to be huge,” manager Dave Roberts said. “He clearly understands that.”
Josue De Paula is making a strong case for making the postseason roster, as the 21-year-old rookie is slashing .323/.500/.581 while becoming the first Dodger rookie with at least a .500 on-base percentage over his first 11 games since Corey Seager in 2015.
De Paula has spent the bulk of his time in the big leagues serving as the designated hitter, filling the void Ohtani left behind. With Ohtani expected to return from the injured list on Wednesday, the next test for De Paula is to see how he can handle himself in the outfield defensively, per Maddie Lee of the Los Angeles Times.
“All the reports that we’ve gotten from our minor-league staff are right on cue,” Ebel said. “He’s been working, he’s bringing it right here to the major leagues. And it’s a pleasure for me, with some energy, coming out early every day — hasn’t missed. We’re working on game situations, ground balls, left, right, right at him, fly balls, shags during BP. So we’re on the right track.”

item.content:encoded:
What Shohei Ohtani's impending return means for Dodgers' lineup
Shohei Ohtani is expected to be activated from the injured list on Wednesday, Sept. 23, manager Dave Roberts told reporters on Tuesday, Sept. 22. If that holds true, it would mean the Los Angeles Dodgers' franchise cornerstone would have five games to ramp up before the start of the postseason.
Ohtani, who has been on the 15-day IL retroactively since Sept. 8 due to lingering issues with his right bicep and left knee, took coach pitch batting practice and went through his normal workout routine on Tuesday ahead of a 7-0 win over the San Diego Padres and according to the Dodgers skipper, he continues to check all the boxes necessary for a return.
"The thought is tomorrow," Roberts told reporters. "Unless I hear otherwise, he'll be in the lineup tomorrow."
The Dodgers have gotten hot in Ohtani's absence, posting an 8-3 record since Sept. 11 – the day he was placed on the IL – and outscoring their opponents 59-28 in that timeframe. They enter Wednesday on a five-game winning streak, have already won the NL West and their magic number to clinch a first-round bye is down to 1. Ohtani will have the opportunity to find his footing in low-stakes games to finish out the regular season. That's huge considering he did not face live pitching in his hitting progression. But what does his impending return mean for the rest of the Dodgers lineup?
Catcher Eliezer Alfonzo was optioned on Tuesday as center fielder Andy Pages made his return. Alex Freeland could be a candidate to get optioned with rookie Josue De Paula, who is in the middle of an impressive "trial run" in his first shot at the big leagues and making a serious push at making the playoff roster. If he does play in October, it would likely be as a lefty bat off the bench.
Dalton Rushing, who has been on the IL since Sept. 6 with right elbow discomfort, is also expected to be activated soon and will battle with De Paula for that spot over the final five games, though Roberts acknowledged that Rushing is at a disadvantage with a small window to show what he can do.
"It’s not a knock on him," Roberts told reporters. "He’s been great for us. but it’s still tough given that also you’re talking about the consistency of at-bats recently from Josue. We have to have those conversations and make a decision."
Whatever the decision ends up being, a red-hot Dodgers offense with Ohtani at the top of it – though Roberts has said he'd consider keeping Mookie Betts batting leadoff against lefties – suddenly makes them one of the toughest matchups this October just when they were looking like they were in their most vulnerable state just weeks ago.

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers extend home winning streak to 11 with shutout of Padres
(Photo credit: William Liang)
Freddie Freeman drove in three runs, Will Smith and Tommy Edman hit home runs and the Los Angeles Dodgers inched closer to the best record in the National League with a 7-0 victory over the visiting San Diego Padres in the opener of a three-game series Tuesday.
Eight Dodgers pitchers held down the red-hot Padres offense in a bullpen game, with Justin Wrobleski (12-5) earning the win. Roki Sasaki struck out two in one inning in his return from a blister issue. The Dodgers extended their home winning streak to 11 games.
Los Angeles fell one game behind the NL-best Milwaukee Brewers and reduced its magic number for a top-two NL spot and a bye into the NL Division Series to one.
Rookie designated hitter Josue De Paula had two hits with a run scored for the Dodgers, with Shohei Ohtani expected to return from a biceps injury as a hitter Wednesday.
Luis Campusano had two hits for the Padres, whose magic number to clinch a playoff spot remained at two. Right-hander Michael King (12-10) gave up five runs on six hits over four innings, his most runs allowed in a start since May 30.
It was just the second loss in 15 games for San Diego, which is close to locking up a third consecutive playoff berth for the first time in franchise history.
The Dodgers took advantage of King's loss of command to start a four-run outburst in the second inning, all with two outs. The Dodgers loaded the bases on two singles and a hit batter, while Edman and Mookie Betts both walked to force in runs.
Freeman followed Betts with a two-run single for a 4-0 lead.
Freeman added a run-scoring single in the fourth inning, while Edman hit a home run in the sixth and Smith hit his in the seventh. Edman homered for the second straight game, while Smith went deep in his third consecutive start.
'The Dodgers welcomed back Andy Pages from a broken left hand, and he was hit by a pitch and drew a walk in four plate appearances.
--Field Level Media

item.title: [ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos] Dodgers score 5 two-out runs off Padres starter Michael King in 7-0 victory

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers score 5 two-out runs off Padres starter Michael King in 7-0 victory
Tommy Edman and Will Smith homered as the Los Angeles Dodgers scored six runs with two outs to beat the San Diego Padres 7-0 in a series opener between rivals with the two best records in the majors this month
LOS ANGELES -- Tommy Edman and Will Smith homered as the Los Angeles Dodgers scored six runs with two outs to beat the San Diego Padres 7-0 on Tuesday night in a series opener between rivals with the two best records in the majors this month.
The Dodgers (97-60) moved within one game of NL Central champion Milwaukee (98-59) for the top mark in the big leagues and home-field advantage throughout the postseason. However, the Brewers own the head-to-head tiebreaker.
Los Angeles needs one win or an Atlanta loss to clinch a first-round bye into a National League Division Series.
The NL West champion Dodgers improved to 15-5 in September with their fifth straight victory; the Padres fell to 14-5 and had their five-game winning streak snapped.
San Diego is tied with Chicago and Philadelphia at 87-70 for the three NL wild cards — four games ahead of Arizona with five to play.
Fernando Tatis Jr. and Manny Machado were a combined 1 for 7 with five strikeouts for the Padres.
The Dodgers chased Michael King (12-10) after four innings in his career-high 32nd start of the season. The right-hander gave up five runs on six hits and struck out five as his four-game winning streak ended.
Los Angeles broke out with four runs in the second. King got the first two outs on six pitches before loading the bases. Teoscar Hernández and rookie Josue De Paula hit consecutive singles before King plunked Andy Pages, who just came off the injured list.
King then issued back-to-back walks to Edman and Mookie Betts, forcing in two runs. Freddie Freeman's two-run single made it 4-0.
Betts had a ground-rule double and scored on Freeman's two-out single for a 5-0 lead in the fourth.
Edman's solo shot came with two outs in the sixth and Smith added a 396-foot drive with one out in the seventh for a 7-0 lead.
Brock Stewart started a bullpen game and Justin Wrobleski (12-5) got the win for the Dodgers, who used eight pitchers to earn the fifth shutout in franchise history when deploying at least that many.
Among them was reliever Edwin Díaz, who struck out two in one inning. Roki Sasaki's four-seam fastball touched 100 mph while he pitched one inning. The Japanese right-hander came off the injured list earlier Tuesday after missing nearly a month with a blister on his right middle finger.
Padres LHP Robbie Ray (13-8, 3.60 ERA) starts Wednesday against Dodgers RHP Yoshinobu Yamamoto (14-8, 2.51).
___
This story has been corrected to show the Dodgers scored six runs with two outs, not five.
___

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Shohei Ohtani to return from IL Wednesday, but Dodgers still have unanswered questions in final week

item.content:encoded:
Shohei Ohtani to return from IL Wednesday, but Dodgers still have unanswered questions in final week
- Click here to listen to this article
-
The Dodgers have less than a week left of the regular season to round into playoff form. And their roster moves this series reflect that time crunch.
Manager Dave Roberts confirmed Tuesday afternoon that Shohei Ohtani (right biceps, left knee) was on track to be reinstated from the 15-day injured list on Wednesday. Ohtani is feeling “considerably” better than he was before the IL stint, according to Roberts.
“I would say if he was a five, he’s probably an eight or a nine right now,” Roberts said before eight pitchers led the Dodgers’ 7-0 win against the San Diego Padres.
On Tuesday, they returned two other important postseason pieces, reinstating center fielder Andy Pages (fractured left hand) and right-hander Roki Sasaki (right middle finger blister) from the injured list.
In corresponding moves, the Dodgers optioned right-hander Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliézer Alfonzo to triple-A Oklahoma City.
Sasaki took the fourth inning of the bullpen game and threw scoreless ball. He gave up a pair of singles, but his fastball had a little extra life in the short stint, averaging 98.7 mph and topping out at 101.7.
Pages went 0 for 2 but reached base twice, on a hit by pitch and a walk.
Even as players return, however, there are still questions the Dodgers have to answer in the last week of the season:
Where will Ohtani hit?
At least at first, Roberts plans to write Ohtani in at the top of the order, per usual. But shortstop Mookie Betts has entered the conversation.
“Certainly versus right-handed pitching [Ohtani] will be there,” Roberts said. “I do think I should think through the Mookie versus left situation, but I have to think about the entire lineup structure.”
Ohtani has hit leadoff in every game he’s started this year. But he hit No. 2 in 79 games the two previous seasons combined.
Even without Ohtani, the Dodgers lineup has been clicking. On Tuesday, Tommy Edman hit his second home run in as many games, and Will Smith homered for the third time in four days.
Is the rotation healthy?
Dodgers left-hander Blake Snell, who exited his start last week with left groin tightness, threw a bullpen on Tuesday. He’s scheduled for one final regular-season start Saturday, Roberts said.
That means all four of the Dodgers’ projected playoff starters are lined up to pitch this Wednesday through Saturday, with Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tyler Glasnow on the mound for the last two games against the Padres, and Tarik Skubal and Snell in the first two games in San Francisco.
Who is the closer?
In short, it could change by the day.
“In a perfect world, as we all know the world’s not perfect, I would love [a set closer],” Roberts said. “I think if there’s an opportunity, for example, for Tanner [Scott] to pitch a high-leverage inning in the seventh or the eighth inning, it’s just hard to pass that up if he’s the best option right there. Because you just don’t know where the ninth inning is going to be.
“Those are things that you have to kind of toil with, and those are always good things for people to debate. Right now I don’t see a one-person closer.”
Sasaki stepped into that role last year. It’s unclear exactly how Roberts will use him this time around, but Roberts said he could be an option, depending on how he pitches coming off the IL.
“Last year it was one of those things where it was a situation of need, as far as where we were at with performance and health and guys,” Roberts said. “He filled that role admirably.”
Who gets the last bench spot?
The battle to serve as the left-handed bat off the bench in the postseason has come down to rookie Josue De Paula and injured catcher Dalton Rushing (right flexor strain). But with Rushing still on the IL, De Paula appears to have an edge.
Don’t read too much into the Dodgers’ corresponding move for Ohtani on Wednesday. If they option De Paula 10 days out from the first game of the National League Division Series, he can still be included on the roster.
The Dodgers will have to make another roster move later in the week, when they plan to activate Rushing. If they option a player to make room for Rushing, that player would only be eligible for the start of the NLDS as the corresponding transaction for an IL move.

item.title: [MLB.com] Sasaki vuelve como relevista mientras Dodgers evalúan su bullpen para octubre
item.dc:creator: Sonja Chen
item.description: LOS ÁNGELES -- Roki Sasaki llamó la atención cuando pasó al bullpen durante la marcha del año pasado hacia el bicampeonato. Volverá a desempeñar ese papel en los últimos días de esta temporada regular y posiblemente vuelva a estar entre las opciones para cerrar juegos. item.content:encoded:
LOS ÁNGELES -- Roki Sasaki llamó la atención cuando pasó al bullpen durante la marcha del año pasado hacia el bicampeonato. Volverá a desempeñar ese papel en los últimos días de esta temporada regular y posiblemente vuelva a estar entre las opciones para cerrar juegos.
Sasaki fue activado de la lista de lesionados de 15 días antes de la victoria por 7-0 sobre los Padres la noche del martes, como parte de una serie de movimientos que también incluyeron el regreso del cubano Andy Pagés de la lista de lesionados y el envío de Emmet Sheehan y el venezolano Eliezer Alfonzo a Triple-A Oklahoma City. Sasaki lanzó por última vez el 26 de agosto, cuando una ampolla en el dedo medio de la mano derecha puso fin prematuramente a su apertura contra los Bravos.
En su segunda temporada en Grandes Ligas, Sasaki se acercaba cada vez más a la versión de sí mismo que fue un fenómeno en la Liga Japonesa de Béisbol Profesional (NPB, por sus siglas en inglés). Tuvo marca de 5-5 con efectividad de 4.60 en 23 aperturas, pero esos números no cuentan toda la historia. Con un repertorio más amplio, que incluye un nuevo splitter, y una mayor velocidad en su recta, Sasaki tuvo su mejor tramo sostenido como abridor en Grandes Ligas, registrando efectividad de 2.63 en siete aperturas antes de lidiar con la ampolla.
“Emocionado de tener a Roki de vuelta”, dijo el manager Dave Roberts. “Está entusiasmado con este rol. Creo que puede tener un gran impacto, como lo tuvo el año pasado”.
En su regreso al bullpen el martes, Sasaki ponchó a dos en un cuarto inning en blanco, pese a permitir un par de sencillos con dos outs. Generó cuatro swings fallidos, incluidos dos en igual número de swings contra su splitter, y promedió 98.7 mph con las ocho rectas que lanzó, ligeramente por encima de su promedio de 97.8 mph esta temporada.
Los Dodgers mejoraron su récord a 97-60 después de que su juego de bullpen terminara en blanqueada. Están cinco juegos por delante de los Bravos en la lucha por el segundo mejor récord de la Liga Nacional y a uno de los Cerveceros, líderes del circuito y dueños del criterio de desempate entre ambos.
El año pasado, el traslado de Sasaki al relevo fue una decisión sin precedentes. Después de un comienzo por debajo de las expectativas en su temporada de novato y de perderse más de cuatro meses por una lesión en el hombro, la única oportunidad de Sasaki de contribuir con los Dodgers en la postemporada era pasar al bullpen.
Sasaki no sólo contribuyó, sino que se convirtió en el cerrador de los Dodgers en la postemporada, permitiendo apenas una carrera limpia en 10.2 innings, para efectividad de 0.84. La confianza que adquirió al conseguir resultados en Grandes Ligas, bajo la máxima presión, impulsó el regreso del derecho de 24 años a la rotación y su posterior despegue a mitad de esta temporada.
Actualmente, los Dodgers no cuentan con un cerrador fijo, ya que el boricua Edwin Díaz está lanzando en situaciones de baja presión en medio de sus dificultades a lo largo de la temporada, mientras busca ganarse un puesto en el bullpen para la postemporada. Díaz ponchó a dos en un quinto inning perfecto la noche del martes, su tercera presentación sin permitir carreras desde que regresó de la lista de lesionados.
Ha pasado mucho tiempo desde que Sasaki lanzó como relevista, pero si logra mostrarle lo suficiente a Roberts durante la última semana antes de la postemporada, podría convertirse en una opción para situaciones de salvamento.
“Creo que sin duda es una opción”, dijo Roberts. “Probablemente mucho dependerá de cómo lance esta noche. Seguramente tendrá una o dos presentaciones cortas más antes de que termine la temporada”.
Con Díaz perdiendo tiempo de juego por lesiones en el codo y el cuello, además de no lanzar bien cuando estuvo saludable, el zurdo Tanner Scott ha recibido la mayoría de las oportunidades de salvamento. Scott lidera a los Dodgers con 23 rescates, pero también ha desperdiciado cuatro oportunidades, incluidas dos desde comienzos de septiembre.
Scott todavía podría ser la mejor opción para cerrar los juegos, pero Sasaki podría complementarlo desde el lado derecho, algo importante debido a que el derecho venezolano Edgardo Henríquez estará fuera por el resto de la temporada regular debido a una distensión en la parte baja de la espalda. Se espera que regrese durante la postemporada.
Aunque a Roberts le gustaría contar con un cerrador en la postemporada, reconoció que es más probable que maneje el bullpen según los enfrentamientos. En esta época del año, algunas de las situaciones de mayor presión se presentan antes del noveno inning, por lo que tener varias opciones le permitiría utilizar a sus mejores relevistas en los momentos más convenientes.
“Creo que si hay una oportunidad, por ejemplo, de que Tanner lance un inning de alta presión en el séptimo u octavo, es difícil dejarla pasar si es la mejor opción en ese momento”, dijo Roberts. “Porque simplemente no sabes cómo se va a presentar el noveno inning”.

item.title: [True Blue LA] Dodgers rout Padres in bulk in opener
item.dc:creator: Eric Stephen

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — On a night the Los Angeles Queens won a championship in the inaugural season of the Women’s Pro Baseball League, the Los Angeles Dodgers beat a King. Four runs with two outs in the second inning off Michael King paced a 7-0 win for the Dodgers over the San Diego Padres in Tuesday night’s series opener at Dodger Stadium.
With the win, the Dodgers are up five games on the Atlanta Braves for the No. 2 seed in the National League playoffs, with five games remaining in the regular season. The Dodgers’ magic number to clinch a bye into the NLDS is down to just one.
King hadn’t allowed more than three runs in any of his previous nine starts, with a 2.26 ERA during that span, and he retired his first five batters faced on Tuesday. Then with two outs in the second inning, the next six batters reached, breaking open the scoring.
Teoscar Hernández singles for the Dodgers’ first hit, then Josue De Paula singled on an 0-2 pitch before Andy Pages was hit by a pitch in his very first plate appearance back since getting hit by a pitch one month prior, to load the bases. Tommy Edman walked on four pitches for the game’s first run, Mookie Betts only needed five pitches to walk home another run, then Freddie Freeman grounded a single through the infield, and under the legs of a leaping Edman, to score two more.
Betts hit a ground-rule double in the fourth, followed by another RBI single by Freeman for a fifth run against King.
Solo home runs by Edman in the sixth and Will Smith in the seventh off the Padres bullpen padded the scoring.
With Emmet Sheehan optioned on Tuesday and Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list, the Dodgers have only three active pitchers they plan to use as starting pitchers in the postseason at the moment. That means they have 11 relievers, and on a day following an off day and the day before a start by the MLB leader in innings per start, the Dodgers used .. pitchers to cover the nine innings.
Starters Justin Wrobleski and Roki Sasaki — the latter just activated on Tuesday — each pitched only one inning, both scoreless. Sasaki was hitting 100 mph in his first game action in four weeks.
Kyle Hurt was the only Dodgers pitcher to toss more than one inning, taking care of the sixth and seventh.
Jack Dreyer was the first pitcher of Sunday’s game, and the last pitcher on Tuesday.
It’s only the third time in franchise history the Dodgers used eight pitchers in a shutout of no more than nine innings, done also on September 29, 2019 in San Francisco and May 15 this year in Anaheim. For some perspective, when the Dodgers beat the Expos 1-0 Montreal in 22 innings on August 23, 1989 — Rick Dempsey homered, Tommy Lasorda got Expos mascot Youppi ejected — the Dodgers only used five pitchers that day.
Tuesday particulars
Home runs: Tommy Edman (8), Will Smith (10)
WP — Justin Wrobleski (12-5): 1 IP, 1 hit
LP — Michael King (12-10): 4 IP, 6 hits, 5 runs, 2 walks, 5 strikeouts

item.title: [tsn.ca] Ohtani 'considerably' healthier, expected back in Dodgers' lineup Wednesday
item.dc:creator: Alden Gonzalez

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- Shohei Ohtani is expected to return to the lineup Wednesday, the first day he is eligible to be activated off the injured list, and Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts says he looks "considerably" healthier than he did a couple of weeks ago.
"If he was a five, he's probably an eight or a nine right now," Roberts said, referencing a 1-to-10 scale.
The Dodgers activated right-hander Roki Sasaki and center fielder Andy Pages off the IL on Tuesday, a major development in the leadup to October.
Sasaki, who has been recovering from a blister suffered in an Aug. 26 start, was available out of the bullpen for Tuesday's series opener against the San Diego Padres and could be an option to again close out games in the postseason. Pages, who fractured his left hand on Aug. 22, will reprise his role as an everyday player at a premium position.
Ohtani landed on the IL because of lingering pain in his right biceps and left knee on Sept. 8 but began a hitting progression seven days ago and advanced to taking as many as 40 swings off Trajekt, the popular pitching simulator, on Saturday. Ohtani also ran the bases that day. On Tuesday, he went through his typical pregame workout.
Ohtani, 32, will only hit the rest of this season and was struggling in that realm before landing on the IL, compiling only seven hits and 22 strikeouts over his past 54 at-bats. Roberts previously indicated the plan was for Ohtani to play in all of the Dodgers' remaining five regular-season games to get reacclimated to major league pitching.
Where he hits, though, is up for debate. In all likelihood, Ohtani will continue to lead off against opposing right-handed pitchers. But Mookie Betts' recent hot streak -- heading into this week, he was hitting.373/.468/.746 in September -- has Roberts weighing the possibility of batting him leadoff against lefties.
What Ohtani's return means for outfield prospect Josue De Paula is also an open question.
De Paula, 21, has eight hits and 10 walks in 38 plate appearances since temporarily replacing Ohtani at designated hitter. The Dodgers are strongly considering him as an option to be a left-handed bat off the bench during the postseason, though they might send him down as the corresponding move for activating Ohtani to give him at-bats in this week's Triple-A championship series.
The other candidate would be backup catcher Dalton Rushing, who has an elbow injury that is preventing him from throwing. Rushing is expected to be activated at some point in the next three days, but Roberts acknowledged it would be difficult for him to be thrust into a pinch-hitting role in October after playing in only four games since the start of September.
"There's potential slug with both those guys," Roberts said. "It's going to be a good debate."

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Roki Sasaki Could Close for Dodgers in Postseason
item.dc:creator: Los Royers
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CA — Roki Sasaki could pitch his way into the Los Angeles Dodgers’ closer conversation before the postseason begins. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA — Roki Sasaki could pitch his way into the Los Angeles Dodgers’ closer conversation before the postseason begins.
Manager Dave Roberts confirmed Tuesday that using Sasaki as a closer in October is an option, although the Dodgers have not assigned him the ninth inning—or any fixed relief role—as he returns from the injured list.
“It’s certainly an option,” Roberts said. “A lot of it probably is contingent on how he throws here tonight.”
Sasaki was activated with Andy Pages before the Dodgers opened their series against the San Diego Padres. Rather than returning to the rotation, the right-hander will spend the final week auditioning for a postseason bullpen role.
Dodgers will evaluate Sasaki in multiple roles
Roberts said Sasaki could work two innings in his first appearance, entering at the start of a clean inning. That opportunity could arrive early, in the middle innings or late in the game depending on how the matchup develops.
“I could envision him pitching multiples,” Roberts said. “I can see him coming into a clean inning and pitching two innings. I’m not sure if that’s the third inning or the sixth inning or the eighth inning, but he’s ready.”
The Dodgers then expect to give Sasaki one or two shorter appearances before the regular season ends. Those outings will help determine whether he can handle a traditional closing assignment, provide multiple innings or fill another high-leverage role in October.
Roberts stopped short of labeling Sasaki the closer and noted that his late-inning success last season developed from the Dodgers’ needs at the time.
“I don’t want to say he’s going to finish games or be a closer,” Roberts said. “Last year was one of those things where it was a situation of need, as far as where we were at with performance, with health of guys, and he filled that role admirably.”
Dodgers do not have a designated closer
Sasaki’s opportunity comes as the Dodgers prepare to enter October without one reliever locked into the ninth inning. Roberts said he would prefer a set closer in a perfect scenario, but he does not currently see one pitcher holding that job.
“Right now, I don’t see a one-person closer,” Roberts said.
That approach would allow Roberts to deploy Tanner Scott against the most dangerous portion of an opponent’s lineup before the ninth rather than saving him for a lead that might never materialize. Roberts also said he would be comfortable asking Evan Phillips or Brock Stewart to close a game.
Phillips has looked more like himself over his last three appearances following an inconsistent beginning to his return from Tommy John surgery, according to Roberts. Stewart has also been one of the Dodgers’ most effective relievers when healthy.
The Dodgers therefore have several ninth-inning possibilities. Sasaki’s final regular-season appearances will determine whether he becomes one of their most prominent options.

item.title: [MLB.com] Pages returns from IL, solidifying Dodgers' defense just in time for October
item.dc:creator: Courtney Hollmon
item.description: LOS ANGELES -- The Dodgers got their center fielder back on Tuesday, but they aren't expecting Andy Pages to immediately pick up where he left off at the plate. And right now, they don't necessarily need him to. When Los Angeles activated Pages from the 10-day injured list ahead of Tuesday’s series opener against the San Diego Padres -- optioning Eliezer Alfonzo in a corresponding move -- it brought an end to a month-long absence caused by a fractured left hand. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- The Dodgers got their center fielder back on Tuesday, but they aren't expecting Andy Pages to immediately pick up where he left off at the plate. And right now, they don't necessarily need him to.
When Los Angeles activated Pages from the 10-day injured list ahead of Tuesday’s series opener against the San Diego Padres -- optioning Eliezer Alfonzo in a corresponding move -- it brought an end to a month-long absence caused by a fractured left hand. With just six regular-season games remaining before the postseason, Pages’ primary task isn't carrying the offense. It's solidifying the outfield defense.
Pages sustained the fracture on Aug. 21 and underwent a minor surgical procedure to insert a compression screw, an intervention designed to accelerate the bone's healing process. While his recovery stayed on track medically, his physical buildup happened almost entirely in isolation.
Because the Triple-A season concluded over the weekend and internal live-pitching options were unavailable at Dodger Stadium, Pages did not face live arms before being thrown back into Major League action. The Dodgers' Minor League affiliates were deep into playoff runs, and injured internal arms were not far enough along to throw live batting practice, leaving Pages to prepare solely through machine work and a simulated game on Saturday.
Front-hand fractures are notoriously difficult for hitters to bounce back from immediately, as the lead hand controls bat path and turn-through at contact. Because of those physical constraints and the lack of live game reps, expectations for Pages' offensive production over this final week are tempered. Before going down, he was having a standout season, batting .272 (including a .288 mark in August) with an .796 OPS and tying Shohei Ohtani for the team lead with 80 RBIs.
Replicating that midseason rhythm at the plate right away is an unrealistic expectation. But while the Dodgers expect his timing against Major League pitching to take a few games to surface, his defensive value is immediate and undeniable.
According to Statcast metrics on Baseball Savant, Pages ranks in the 94th percentile among qualified defenders with eight outs above average. He has transformed center field into a strength for Los Angeles. In the postseason, where run prevention often dictates close games, having a trusted glove in center field provides a massive floor for manager Dave Roberts -- regardless of how the bats fare.
"The defense is a big reason why he’s still a valuable player, even coming off the IL, with the uncertainty of the offense, which we’ll still bet on," manager Dave Roberts said. "But playing a premium position and playing it well is hugely important."
Physically, the team feels comfortable throwing him right back into the fire. While Roberts acknowledged on Saturday that balancing Pages' workload over six straight games would require careful monitoring, he noted on Tuesday that Pages' lower-half conditioning puts him in a good spot to play full games right away.
"I think that I feel good with him playing nine," Roberts said. "He's worked real hard on his lower half, his legs, conditioning, all that stuff. So if I have to manage him, we could do that pivot, get him out of there, get somebody in there to play defense, things like that. But I think right now, the thought is for him to play out each game."

item.title: [MLB.com] Sasaki returns in relief role as Dodgers assess bullpen options for postseason
item.dc:creator: Sonja Chen

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- Roki Sasaki opened eyes when he moved to the bullpen for last year's run to back-to-back championships. He'll reprise that role in the final days of this regular season -- and possibly be in the mix to close out games once again.
Sasaki was activated from the 15-day injured list ahead of Tuesday night's series opener against the Padres amid a flurry of moves that also saw Andy Pages return from the IL and Emmet Sheehan and Eliezer Alfonzo get optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City. Sasaki last pitched on Aug. 26, when a blister on his right middle finger brought his start against the Braves to a premature end.
In his second Major League season, Sasaki was steadily growing closer to resembling the version of himself who was a phenom in Nippon Professional Baseball. He went 5-5 with a 4.60 ERA through 23 starts, but those numbers don't tell the full story. Working with an expanded pitch mix, including a new splitter, and increased fastball velocity, Sasaki put together his best sustained stretch as an MLB starter, recording a 2.63 ERA through seven starts before dealing with the blister.
"Excited to see Roki back," manager Dave Roberts said. "He's looking forward to this role. I think he can be very impactful, as it was last year."
In his return to the bullpen on Tuesday, Sasaki was available to pitch multiple innings. He will likely get a couple of additional relief appearances in the final five games of the regular season.
Last year, Sasaki's shift to relief was an unprecedented move. After underperforming to begin his rookie season and then missing more than four months with a shoulder injury, Sasaki's only chance to contribute to the Dodgers in the postseason was to move to the 'pen.
Sasaki didn't just contribute -- he became the Dodgers' postseason closer, allowing just one earned run in 10 2/3 innings (0.84 ERA). The confidence he gained from getting results at the big league level, with the stakes as high as could be, fueled the 24-year-old right-hander's return to the rotation and eventual midseason breakout this year.
The Dodgers are currently working without a set closer, as Edwin Díaz is pitching in low leverage amid his season-long struggles as he looks to earn a role in the postseason bullpen. It has been a long time since Sasaki has pitched in relief, but if he can show Roberts enough in the final week before the postseason, he could very well be an option in save situations.
"I think it's certainly an option," Roberts said. "A lot of it, probably, is contingent on how he throws here tonight. He'll probably get another one or two shorter stints before the season's end."
With Díaz missing time with elbow and neck injuries -- and not pitching well when healthy -- left-hander Tanner Scott has gotten the bulk of save opportunities. Scott leads the Dodgers with 23 saves, but he's also blown four saves, including two since the start of September.
Scott may still be the best option to close out games, but Sasaki could complement him from the right-hand side, which is important with leverage righty Edgardo Henriquez out for the rest of the regular season with a lower back strain (he is expected back during the postseason).
While Roberts would like to have a closer in the postseason, he acknowledged that it's more likely that he will play the matchups. At this time of year, some of the highest-leverage situations take place before the ninth inning, so having multiple options would free up Roberts to use his best relievers in the lanes that make sense.
"I think if there's an opportunity, for example, for Tanner to pitch a high-leverage inning in the seventh or the eighth inning, it's just hard to pass that up if he's the best option right there," Roberts said. "Because you just don't know where the ninth inning is going to be."

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have just two series left on their MLB schedule before the playoffs begin next week.
Beginning on Tuesday, the Dodgers will play the San Diego Padres, and in the final weekend of the season, LA will take on the Giants.
However, speaking to Tuesday's game, the Dodgers announced a Kyle Tucker lineup decision before their game one with the Padres.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Announce Emmet Sheehan Demotion Before Padres Series
Kyle Tucker Back in Dodgers Batting Order Hitting 5th
After sitting out for Sunday's game against the Giants, Kyle Tucker is back in the batting order for the Dodgers.
Per @UnderdogMLB, here is the full group:
Dodgers 9/22: "M. Betts SS F. Freeman 1B W. Smith C M. Muncy 3B K. Tucker RF T. Hernández LF J. De Paula DH A. Pages CF T. Edman 2B B. Stewart SP"
Other lineup notes include Josue De Paula getting the nod at DH, Andy Pages being in the lineup after being activated, and Will Smith behind the plate for LA to catch Brock Stewart, who was suddenly announced as the SP for Tuesday's game.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Announce 4 Roster Moves Before Padres Game
Inside Kyle Tucker's Season with the Dodgers
Kyle Tucker is in the middle of his first season with the Dodgers.
It's been a very up-and-down campaign, but Tucker may be hitting a very important stride as October approaches.
He's still batting just .234, but Tucker has 17 home runs now, 70 RBI, and 121 hits over 516 at-bats. His OPS+ is 100, which is exactly league average.
CBSSport.com's RotoWire staff wrote (about Tucker):
"After missing Sunday's series finale against the Giants, Tucker will return to the starting nine for Tuesday's series opener with the Padres. The 29-year-old will bat fifth and man right field for the Dodgers."

item.content:encoded:
LA 다저스는 22일 밤(미국 현지시간) 다저스타디움에서 샌디에이고 파드리스를 상대로 시작되는 중요한 시리즈를 앞두고 타선과 불펜을 보강했습니다.
다저스는 화요일 외야수 앤디 파헤스와 우완 투수 사사키 로키를 부상자 명단에서 해제했습니다. 이에 따른 후속 조치로 우완 투수 에밋 시한과 포수 엘리에세르 알폰소가 트리플A로 내려갔습니다.
앤디 파헤스는 지난 8월 21일 투구에 맞아 왼쪽 손가락 골절 부상을 당하기 전까지 타율 0.272, 홈런 21개, 도루 12개, OPS 0.796을 기록하고 있었습니다. 그는 회복 과정을 앞당기기 위해 나사 삽입 수술을 받았으며, 별도의 마이너리그 재활 경기 출전 없이 곧바로 부상자 명단에서 해제되었습니다. 다만 19일에 열린 확장 시뮬레이션 경기를 소화했습니다.
사사키 로키는 지난 8월 27일부터 오른쪽 손가락 가운데 물집 증세로 전력에서 이탈해 있었습니다. 그 역시 재활 경기를 거치지 않았지만, 16일에 4이닝 동안 48개의 공을 던진 시뮬레이션 경기를 포함해 최근 실전 타자들을 상대로 투구를 소화했습니다. 원래 계획은 선발 투수로 몸 상태를 다시 끌어올리는 것이었으나, 사사키는 정규시즌 마지막 날들에 다저스의 불펜 요원으로 대기할 예정입니다. 그는 이번 시즌 119.1이닝을 던지며 평균자책점 4.60을 기록하고 있습니다.
이번 선수단 활성화 조치는 다저스가 오타니 쇼헤이까지 복귀시킬 수 있는 시점을 단 하루 앞두고 이루어졌습니다. 오타니는 수요일에 부상자 명단에서 해제될 자격을 얻게 되며, 데이브 로버츠 감독은 일요일 인터뷰에서 오타니가 그때 라인업에 복귀할 "좋은 기회"가 있다고 시사했습니다. 왼쪽 무릎과 오른쪽 이두근 통증에 시달려 온 오타니는 남은 시즌 동안 마운드에 오르지 않을 것입니다.
96승 60패를 기록 중인 다저스는 내셔널리그 플레이오프 2번 시드 자리를 두고 브레이브스에 4경기 차로 앞서 있으며, 이 순위를 유지하면 다저스는 디비전 시리즈에 직행하게 됩니다. 만약 오늘 시즌이 종료된다면, LA 다저스는 3번 시드 애틀랜타 브레이브스와 6번 시드 필라델피아 필리스 간의 내셔널리그 와일드카드 시리즈 승자와 홈 경기를 치르게 됩니다.
그러나 필리스(86승 70패)가 컵스 및 파드리스(나란히 87승 69패)에 불과 1경기 차로 바짝 추격하고 있어 내셔널리그 와일드카드 순위 레이스는 여전히 혼전 양상을 보이고 있습니다. 샌디에이고는 최근 5연승 및 지난 14경기 중 13승을 거두는 상승세를 탄 채 화요일 차바트 라빈에 도착했습니다.

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Dave Roberts' Hyeseong Kim update confirms Dodgers' position battle never really ended

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are still fighting to keep their first-round bye, but they're already prepping for their 14th consecutive postseason appearance — and there are a number of questions they still need to answer.
Will Shohei Ohtani be ready? Does Edwin Díaz make the roster? Will Andy Pages be available? Is Roki Sasaki ready to return to his role as the Dodgers' vaunted postseason closer?
Every option to try to make up for these weaknesses is being considered. Even Hyeseong Kim, who has spent the majority of this season at Triple-A Oklahoma City.
"My expectation is Hyeseong will be here during the off-week and potentially be a conversation for the postseason — because he has the ability to run, play defense, and steal a base," Dave Roberts said, "So he's in the conversation, yes."
Alex Freeland is probably the most dispensable player on the Dodgers' active roster. If he's left behind, it'll be proof that their second base battle never truly declared a winner.
Dave Roberts hints at Hyeseong Kim return for Dodgers' postseason run
Kim was last seen in the majors from early April to late May. He was initially called up to replace Mookie Betts who went onto the injured list with an oblique strain. Kim hit .259 with a .651 OPS before being sent back down. His numbers in Triple-A have been nothing to write home about either (.675 OPS).
But Kim was on the Dodgers' postseason roster last season. His contributions were few — he earned a pinch-running appearance in the NLDS and was a defensive substitution during the World Series — and he didn't pick up a bat.
But Freeland is hot, and is hitting .375 with a 1.149 OPS over his last seven games. His ability to get on-base, the attribute that really put him on the map to begin with, has slowly come back to him. He has a .413 on-base percentage in September.
Clearly, this is a conversation the Dodgers are going to have to continue unless they trade one or both of these players. If Kim and Freeland survive the offseason together, they'll probably have to do it all over again next year.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are opening up for a blockbuster series, their last big test, against the San Diego Padres.
Dodgers Lineup
1. Mookie Betts, SS
2. Freddie Freeman, 1B
3. Will Smith, C
4. Max Muncy, 3B
5. Kyle Tucker, RF
6. Teoscar Hernandez, LF
7. Josue De Paula, DH
8. Andy Pages, CF
9. Tommy Edman, 2B
Andy Pages is back in the batting order after being activated from the injured list. He broke his hand after getting hit by a pitch, had surgery, and after a month on the shelf, he is back.
It may take some time for him to shake off the rust at the plate, but his defense should not skip a beat.
The Dodgers are facing righty Michael King, but many of the hottest bats are righties.
Mookie Betts, Will Smith, and Kyle Tucker are among the most dialed-in hitters, and they should drive most of the offense.
Ideally, Freddie Freeman gets going again, since he hasn’t looked right in a while.
Who’s pitching for the Dodgers
The Dodgers will have Brock Stewart as the opener, with Roki Sasaki getting the bulk of the work out of the bullpen.
On Tuesday, hours before the game, Sasaki was activated off the injured list after recovering from his blister.
Sasaki has been great since the All-Star break, posting a 3.05 ERA with 37 strikeouts and 15 walks.
His splitter and slider are fantastic, while the fastball has been the difference-maker, showing some renewed life.
The Japanese righty is set to enter the bullpen in a varied role, either stepping in for a struggling starter or pitching late in high-leverage spots.
Stewart, meanwhile, has been a bit lucky, with a 2.55 ERA and a 3.91 FIP.
FanGraphs’ pitching models have appreciated his stuff and command, and while he has pitched better lately, he is prone to giving up hard contact.

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

23 Sep 2026, 02:10 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Kirby Lee)
The Los Angeles Dodgers activated a pair of key contributors in advance of a marquee series against the San Diego Padres, bringing back center fielder Andy Pages and right-hander Roki Sasaki from the injured list.
In corresponding moves, right-hander Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliezer Alfonzo were optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Pages, 25, has not played since Aug. 21, when he was hit by a pitch on the left hand from Pittsburgh Pirates right-hander Bubba Chandler. An All-Star for the first time this season, Pages was batting .272 with 21 home runs and 80 RBIs in 128 games.
Sasaki, 24, last pitched Aug. 26 when he developed a blister on his right middle finger in an outing against the Atlanta Braves. He is 5-5 with a 4.60 ERA in 23 outings (all starts) this season and is scheduled to make an abbreviated appearance Tuesday.
Sheehan, 26, started the season in the Los Angeles rotation, was sent down in early August amid ongoing struggles and has returned for three outings this month where he recorded 24 strikeouts over 17 innings. He is 5-8 with a 4.57 ERA in 23 appearances (22 starts) this season.
Sheehan and Sasaki both are projected to have a bullpen role for the Dodgers in the playoffs, according to manager Dave Roberts.
Alfonzo, 26, made his major league debut in July and is batting .179 with four RBIs in 13 career games.
While the Dodgers enter Tuesday's play with a magic number of three to clinch a bye into a National League Division Series matchup, the Padres have a magic number of two to clinch a wild-card spot and a team-record third consecutive playoff appearance.
Also on Tuesday, the Dodgers sold Ryan Ward's contract to the Chunichi Dragons in Japan, according to multiple reports. A longtime minor leaguer, the 28-year-old Ward made his major league debut this season and hit three home runs in 20 games. The former Pacific Coast League MVP was designated for assignment last week.
--Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have activated outfielder Andy Pages and right-handed pitcher Roki Sasaki from the injured list ahead of Tuesday's series opener vs. the Padres and optioned right-handed pitcher Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliezer Alfonzo to Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Pages, 25, has been out since August 21 after fracturing his left hand against the Pirates. The All-Star has played in 128 games, batting .272 with 21 homers and 80 RBI. He is in his third season with the Dodgers and he has played in 400 games with 61 homers and 212 RBI. He was signed by the Dodgers as an international free agent on March 1, 2018 out of La Habana, Cuba.
Sasaki, 24, has been on the injured list since August 27 with a blister on his right middle finger. In his second full season with the Dodgers, he is 5-5 with a 4.60 ERA, including a 2-0 record with a 3.05 ERA since the All-Star break. He has made 33 Major League appearances in his career, posting a 6-6 mark with a 4.57 ERA and 145 strikeouts in 155.2 innings. He joined the Dodgers as an international free agent on January 22, 2025 from Rikuzentakata, Japan.
Sheehan, 26, pitched 5.1 scoreless innings on Sunday against the Giants. He is 5-8 and a 4.57 ERA with the Dodgers in 2026, racking up 132 strikeouts in 112.1 innings. He is in his third season with the Dodgers, recording a 4.13 ERA with a 15-12 record in 51 games (45 starts). He was drafted by the Dodgers in the sixth round of the 2021 First Year Player Draft out of Boston College.
Alfonzo, 26, has played in 13 games for the Dodgers this season, batting .179 with two doubles and four RBI. He was batting .302 with two homers and 25 RBI with Triple-A Oklahoma City this season. He has appeared in 598 minor league games, batting .283 with 33 homers and 291 RBI. He signed with the Dodgers as a minor league free agent on November 17, 2025.

item.title: [True Blue LA] Dodgers activate Andy Pages, Roki Sasaki from injured list
item.dc:creator: Eric Stephen
item.description: LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers on Tuesday got a few regulars back as reinforcements heading into the final week of the regular season and into October, activating center fielder Andy Pages and pitcher Roki Sasaki off the injured list. Pages missed 27 games after getting hit by a fastball on his left hand on August 21. Sasaki left his start in Atlanta five days later with a blister on his right middle finger. Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliezer Alfonzo were optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City on Monday.
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers on Tuesday got a few regulars back as reinforcements heading into the final week of the regular season and into October, activating center fielder Andy Pages and pitcher Roki Sasaki off the injured list.
Pages missed 27 games after getting hit by a fastball on his left hand on August 21. Sasaki left his start in Atlanta five days later with a blister on his right middle finger.
Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliezer Alfonzo were optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City on Monday.
Pages was an All-Star starter this season, and when he got hurt was tied with Yoshinobu Yamamoto for second-highest FanGraphs WAR (3.9) on the team, behind only Shohei Ohtani. By Baseball Reference WAR, Pages is still third on the team now at 5.4, trailing only Ohtani and Yamamoto. That’ll happen with a .272/.338/.458 batting line with a 118 wRC+ combined with plus-defense in center field.
Before getting hit by an errant fastball on August 21, Pages started 125 of the Dodgers’ 129 games, and led the team in plate appearances (550) at the time. Pages and Ohtani are still tied for the Dodgers’ lead with 80 runs batted in. With Pages out, Alek Thomas was first called up to start six games in center field, followed by Tommy Edman starting 17 games, plus three starts by Alex Call and one by Kiké Hernández.
With Edman moving to the outfield and once Thomas was optioned, Miguel Rojas (10) and Alex Freeland (eight) have covered all but one of the starts at second base in September.
Sasaki struggled earlier in the season, but improved as the season progressed. He has a streak of six straight starts with no more than two runs allowed until his blister start in Atlanta. On the season, Sasaki has a 4.46 ERA and 4.42 xERA, but since July 8 he’s down to a 3.25 ERA and 3.76 xERA in eight starts.
With Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, and Tyler Glasnow set for the postseason rotation, the Dodgers will see over the next two weeks if Blake Snell will be hampered by his left groin discomfort, and will have Sheehan at the ready. That allows them to use Sasaki in relief, as they did last postseason out of necessity.
“I could see multiples [innings], but it’s not going to be bulk as in four or five innings,” manager Dave Roberts said on Sunday.
Last season was a different situation for Sasaki, who struggled mightily as a starter and spend four months on the injured list before returning in the final week of the regular season. There was no room in the rotation, so he pitched in relief in the postseason. He wasn’t dominant — only six strikeouts among his 43 batters faced, with five walks — but he was effective, allowing only one run over nine appearances and 10 2/3 innings, the highlight his perfect three innings of relief in the Dodgers’ NLDS Game 4 clincher over the Philadelphia Phillies.
Sasaki saved three games last postseason. Roberts said Sasaki probably wouldn’t get an opportunity in a save situation right away this week, but it could progress to that by the postseason.
“I trust Roki in any situation. I would say probably starting a clean inning,” Roberts said. “He’s done it, he’s really good. He’s a neutral pitcher, high-octane stuff. And you really just need four starters. So we’re in a good spot there, for now.”
Sheehan has been fantastic of late, allowing only one run in three starts for the Dodgers over the previous two weeks, with 24 strikeouts in 17 innings. The plan for Sheehan is to start on Saturday for Oklahoma City should the Comets advance to the Triple-A championship game.
Alfonzo was back with the Dodgers since September 6 when Dalton Rushing was placed on the injured list with elbow soreness. In the 14 games since, Alfonzo played only once, pinch-hitting as the designated hitter at the end of a 14-1 blowout of the Cincinnati Reds. He struck out.
Alfonzo made his major league debut against the Padres on July 5, and started nine games behind the plate. He had five hits in 28 at-bats with three doubles and four runs batted in.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers activated Andy Pages from the 10-day injured list and optioned Eliezer Alfonzo to Triple-A Oklahoma City. The move was made during the off day on Monday, but the Dodgers did not officially announce it at the time.
In addition, Roki Sasaki was also activated while Emmet Sheehan was optioned.
The Dodgers first recalled Alfonzo when Dalton Rushing was placed on the IL on Sept. 6. During his second stint with the club, Alfonzo only received one at-bat, which came against the Cincinnati Reds on Sept. 9 when he struck out.
Alfonzo was the third catcher on the roster, which Dodgers manager Dave Roberts explained was to allow the club to more freely use Will Smith and Hunter Feduccia as pinch-hitters when they didn’t start.
The Dodgers also did not need to make a 40-man roster move to call up Alfonzo, which likely played into their decision.
The 26-year-old has appeared in 13 total games this season, making his MLB debut and batting .179/.179/.250 with four RBI and three runs scored in 28 plate appearances. In Oklahoma City, he was hitting .302/.378/.409 in 256 plate appearances.
Pages is back with the Dodgers for the first time in a month after he landed on the IL with a left hand fracture on Aug. 22.
Pages suffered the injury when he was hit by a pitch from Pittsburgh Pirates starter Bubba Chandler. The 26-year-old underwent surgery shortly after to insert a compression screw in his hand to speed up the healing process.
Pages did not go on a rehab assignment before returning, but did workouts at Dodger Stadium, which included hitting on the field, running the bases, and doing outfield drills.
That makes this stretch of six games important for Pages to face live pitching and get as many at-bats as possible to prepare for the postseason. But even with that in mind, the Dodgers also have to be cautious about building him back up and not overworking him after a month of not playing.
“So we have obviously, assuming he gets back on Tuesday, then there’s six in a row, and that seems pretty aggressive,” Roberts explained.
“So I think that we do want to get him as many at-bats as possible, but we have to make sure that his legs are under him, feeling good, so we don’t go backward or get injured in that respect. So it is going to be a balancing act, and just keeping a keen eye on Andy for sure.”
Pages is batting .272/.338/.458 with 25 doubles, 21 home runs, 80 RBI and 72 runs scored this season. He has also been among the top defensive players in MLB.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] What Andy Pages means to Dodgers’ postseason after returning from injury
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: In too many cases this year, the Dodgers dealt with injuries to players that lasted far longer than they initially anticipated. On Tuesday, however, they got one of their most important bats back right on schedule. The Dodgers have officially activated center fielder Andy Pages, according to MLB's transactions log, adding him back into their lineup for the final week of the regular season. Pages had been out one month, after going on the injured list on Aug. 22 with a hand fracture he suffered f
item.content:encoded:
In too many cases this year, the Dodgers dealt with injuries to players that lasted far longer than they initially anticipated.
On Tuesday, however, they got one of their most important bats back right on schedule.
The Dodgers have officially activated center fielder Andy Pages, according to MLB's transactions log, adding him back into their lineup for the final week of the regular season.
Pages had been out one month, after going on the injured list on Aug. 22 with a hand fracture he suffered from a 100 mph hit-by-pitch. His initial timeline of 4-5 weeks proved accurate, thanks in part to a surgical procedure he underwent to accelerate his recovery process.
The question now is whether Pages will be able to recapture his All-Star form offensively following such a significant injury.
Manager Dave Roberts acknowledged that challenge over the week, saying that while he is still "expecting good at-bats" from the third-year slugger, he was still "waiting just like you guys are waiting to see how it looks."
For many hitters, a broken hand can cause a lack of feel or strength in their swings. The last Dodgers player to endure such an injury was Mookie Betts in 2024, when he went from an MVP candidate beforehand to a below-league-average hitter for not only the rest of that year but 2025, as well.
However, the Dodgers are hopeful in what Pages will be able to provide the rest of the season –– not only with his bat but also his premium glove (and arm) in center field.
This year, Pages leads all MLB outfielders with 13 assists and ranks second among center fielders with 20 defensive runs saved. That alone, Roberts said, is "a big reason why he's still a valuable player, even coming off the IL with the uncertainty of the offense."
As for his offense, the manager added: "We'll still bet on [that, too]."
Pages was in the midst of a career-best season before getting hurt, batting .272 with 21 home runs, 80 RBIs, a .797 OPS and 45 walks (a sharp increase from the 29 he drew in each of his first two big-league campaigns). It was good enough to help him earn a first selection to the Midsummer Classic and a bump up to the No. 2 spot in the Dodgers' batting order.
The 25-year-old had cooled off in the second half, after finishing May batting .294 with 13 long balls. He also didn't get a typical recovery process as a hitter during his time on the IL, unable to go on a minor-league rehab assignment (since the minor-league season was ending as he returned to health) or even face pitching in a live batting session.
Instead, he went through simulated games last week in which he alternated between hitting off a machine at Dodger Stadium and taking reps in center field on balls hit by members of the coaching staff.
Still, the Dodgers are confident he will be able to provide enough all-around production in his return to the active roster now.
"Playing a premium position and playing it well," Roberts said, "is hugely important."

item.title: [dodgersway.com] Dodgers map out Shohei Ohtani return with Roki Sasaki, Andy Pages roster moves

The expectation in recent weeks was that Shohei Ohtani, Andy Pages, and Roki Sasaki would return before the end of the regular season, and the Dodgers quietly revealed the roster moves to map everything out.
