item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are pacing toward having a first-round bye, avoiding the NL Wild Card round, and it would seem they are getting healthy at just the right time. The expectation in recent weeks was that Shohei Ohtani, Andy Pages, and Roki Sasaki would return before the end of the regular season, and the Dodgers quietly revealed the roster moves to map everything out.
Updating their transaction log overnight, the Dodgers have reinstated Pages and Sasaki from the IL, and optioned Emmet Sheehan and Eliezer Alfonzo to the minors. With Ohtani eligible to be reinstated from the IL on Wednesday, the expectation is that Alex Freeland will be the corresponding move.
For Ohtani and Pages, the goal was simply having them back before the start of the playoffs. They now have a runway to shake off the rust over these next handful of games, before likely having next week off before playing in the NLDS.
Circumstances are a little more dire for Sasaki, who hasn't secured a spot on LA's playoff roster. Dave Roberts has already confirmed that Sasaki will be used out of the bullpen upon his return, and it goes to one of the biggest questions facing the Dodgers ahead of the playoffs.
The Dodgers are getting healthy just in time, but there are still answers needed
The Dodgers need to find answers in the bullpen. Ironically, the stage is set for Sasaki to repeat a similar shift he made last season. While the Dodgers have been adamant that Sasaki's future is as a starting pitcher, he was used as a quasi-finisher during the playoffs last year, and thrived.
Considering the questions surrounding Edwin Diaz and Edgardo Henriquez currently dealing with an injury, Sasaki once again becoming an effective high-leverage option for the Dodgers would be a major development for the playoffs.
The story of the Dodgers since the trade deadline has been that they are leaking oil. Sure, they traded for Tarik Skubal, but the operation looked faulty. With the returns of Sasaki, Pages, and Ohtani likely on Wednesday, they are finally reaching a level of healthy they haven't had for most of the season.
In other words, despite how uneven things have looked, the Dodgers are once again in a position to do whay they do best and flip the swith on during the month of October.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers notes: Is this team (and Edwin Diaz) playoff ready?
item.dc:creator: Andy Lane Chapman
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers have managed to work their way out of their usual late summer lull, by going 14-5 so far in the month of September. But they face a test starting Tuesday to see if they really are in postseason form. This month, the Dodgers have beat up on below .500 teams in the Washington Nationals, Cincinnati Reds, and San Francisco Giants. But they have one last team with a winning record to face before the playoffs – the San Diego Padres. The Padres come in to this series winners of
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have managed to work their way out of their usual late summer lull, by going 14-5 so far in the month of September. But they face a test starting Tuesday to see if they really are in postseason form.
This month, the Dodgers have beat up on below .500 teams in the Washington Nationals, Cincinnati Reds, and San Francisco Giants. But they have one last team with a winning record to face before the playoffs – the San Diego Padres.
The Padres come in to this series winners of 13 of their last 14 games, needing two wins to secure a wildcard playoff spot. They have never made the playoffs three seasons in a row in the history of their franchise.
"I feel like the whole team is in a good spot right now," San Diego's Fernando Tatis Jr. told the San Diego Union-Tribune on Sunday. "We're playing really good baseball. We're checking in when we have to. The entire lineup is in a good spot right now. So when it's going like that, it's … a good time."
For their part, the Dodgers have a magic number of three to secure the second bye in the playoffs, which is important in setting the rotation that the Dodgers want.
"I think it's going to be a good kind of (playoff) primer," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of the upcoming series. "They're a very talented team. They're playing as good as anyone in all of baseball. I'm looking forward to playing those guys and just kind of ramping it up a little bit more for our guys."
Andy Pages is expected to be activated off the IL on Tuesday, hopefully fully healed and ready to add to the Dodgers offensive firepower.
Doug Padilla of the OC Register covers more of the details of what the Dodgers are thinking in their last six games of the season here.
One of the things still up in the air as far as the postseason roster goes is the status of Edwin Diaz, and if he can make a positive impact in the playoffs.
Diaz returned from the IL on Friday, a has two scoreless outings. But is that enough to get back on Dave Roberts' trust tree?
"It's been really disappointing," Díaz said of his season. "But now I've found growth to come back and perform the way everyone was expecting."
Diaz was on the IL earlier this season after having surgery on bone chips in his elbow and he came back ready to return to the leverage part of the bullpen. Except he wasn't actually ready.
Katie Woo of The Athletic covers all of the ins and outs of Diaz's return and playoff roster hopes here:
"Everybody was telling me I have a new elbow, so just keep going, keep climbing the ladder," Díaz said. "You will be fine. We trust you. They always stayed positive with me, and you know, I was positive too. I know when I'm right, I can do really good things. I just trusted the process with them. They stuck with me. They supported me. So I was OK."
But he wasn't ok. In his nine outings after returning from the IL, Diaz's ERA swelled to 11.85. He landed back on the IL with neck inflammation. So far in this return, he seems to be doing better. But with only six games left, he only has three to four games to prove he's playoff ready.

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] The Dodgers’ Josue De Paula can hit. Now he’s out to prove he can play defense, too
item.dc:creator: Maddie Lee
item.description: - Click here to listen to this article - Dodgers rookie Josue De Paula sat down with third base and outfield coach Dino Ebel in the visiting coach’s room at Great American Ball Park. Ebel pulled up defensive metrics on three different outfielders. One was Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong, the National League MVP favorite and MLB’s defensive fWAR leader. Another was Dodgers center fielder Andy Pages, who has evolved into an elite center fielder during his time with the organization.
item.content:encoded:
- Click here to listen to this article
-
Dodgers rookie Josue De Paula sat down with third base and outfield coach Dino Ebel in the visiting coach’s room at Great American Ball Park. Ebel pulled up defensive metrics on three different outfielders.
One was Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong, the National League MVP favorite and MLB’s defensive fWAR leader. Another was Dodgers center fielder Andy Pages, who has evolved into an elite center fielder during his time with the organization. And the third was De Paula.
“There’s a lot of colors in the game, and when you have red, it’s not good, and when you have green, it’s good,” Ebel said in a recent conversation with The Times. “And he saw a lot of green from the other two players, and he saw some green and some red on his side. So it kind of hit home with him.”
The reports broke down his first step, going right and left, arm strength, and so on.
For the past 17 years, Chaz Perea and his four-person crew have been responsible for every bit of stadium landscaping that isn’t the field itself.
“Just comparing [Pages’] journey, too, with mine — and that it’s possible,” De Paula said of what he took from the conversation. “I have all the tools under my belt to be able to do so. It’s more about just being focused throughout the whole thing, and having that drive to want to do it.
“And when I saw it, it was also a motivation for me. It was like, all right, let’s go now.”
It was De Paula’s bat that earned him a call-up when Shohei Ohtani landed on the injured list. And it’s his bat that’s now making his case for a postseason roster spot. (“This is more of a trial run,” manager Dave Roberts said last week.)
For De Paula to stick in the majors, however, his development on the defensive side is going to be key. As he has risen through the system, his outfield play has lagged behind his offensive influence. But the Dodgers have already seen growth this year.
“Our goal is to become, one day, a Gold Glover,” Ebel said. “And I think he’s young enough to do it, and his mindset is right, he’s got a chance to do that.”
Dodgers special assistant Jason Heyward started poring over video of the team’s top prospects — a group chalk full of outfielders, led by De Paula — as soon as he began working for the Dodgers’ front office at the beginning of May.
“He handles constructive criticism, for me, with some of the best of them that I’ve been around,” Heyward said.
Heyward, a five-time Gold Glove outfielder, first met De Paula in spring training in 2024, when the prospect jumped in on outfield drills with the major leaguers. In Heyward’s new role, he’s made multiple trips to Tulsa, Okla., to work with De Paula and the rest of the group there.
Heyward emphasized building a consistent and productive routine.
“He makes it so easy to have something to make relatable to this because I’ve seen his work in the cage, I’ve seen his attention to detail,” Heyward said. “He takes on challenges, but it’s not a, ‘Let me hurry up and get to this challenge, let me rush through this.’ He’s like, ‘No, I’m going to go about this how I want to go about it, I’m not going to be rushed, I’m going to lock in, and I’m going to give this like all my focus.’”
That process on the offensive side was something Heyward encouraged De Paula to tap into in all parts of his game, including defense. But De Paula said Heyward also acknowledged that the nature of playing in the outfield can make that more difficult.
“Hitting, you are always unfocused on the next pitch, your mind is always going,” De Paula said. “But you could go three days without getting a fly ball. So it’s kind of easy for your mind to drift and stuff like that. But it’s just more about tips of engagement and that intensity of focus.”
Heyward was a fitting person to deliver the message. Once a heralded prospect for the Braves, he put together a 16-year MLB career that included a second-place rookie of the year finish, an All-Star nod, and a stellar reputation for defense and veteran leadership.
“It’s a blessing to have somebody like that in your corner, especially rooting for you, to be able to see your talent, like what you’re capable of,” De Paula said. “He’s been through it, so he knows, man. So it’s awesome to have somebody like that as your mentor.”
Coincidentally, De Paula would go on to launch a three-run home run as his first major-league hit, a feat he shares with Heyward — although Heyward did it in his first at-bat.
“It’s a very commendable job that all of our staff have done at every level,” Heyward said. “... I’d be doing a big injustice without giving everyone their flowers on this because it’s definitely been a group effort. … For someone like him who became a part of the organization at 16 years old, he’s a Dodger through and through.”
Over the past week and a half, the major-league coaching staff, which also had De Paula in major-league spring training camp the last two years, has taken over. And already, they’ve seen the benefit of the routine he’s developed this year.
“All the reports that we’ve gotten from our minor-league staff are right on cue,” Ebel said. “He’s been working, he’s bringing it right here to the major leagues. And it’s a pleasure for me, with some energy, coming out early every day — hasn’t missed. We’re working on game situations, ground balls, left, right, right at him, fly balls, shags during BP. So we’re on the right track.”
Dodgers two-time Cy Young winner Blake Snell joined them one day in Miami, catching De Paula’s throws in early work. Though the new teammates wanted to keep the specifics of their conversations between them, Snell’s advice and encouragement made an impression — “It’s like putting fuel in a rocket,” De Paula said.
“He’s just really, really talented, lots to learn,” Snell said. “And excited for him in his journey and what it could turn into.”
In the next city, Cincinnati, Roberts spent an afternoon in left field with him while he was shagging fly balls during batting practice.
“I wanted to be up close to watch him get off on the baseball, watch his reads, his angles to balls and make sure he’s shagging the right way,” Roberts said. “Had some instruction for him; he was great.”
Mookie Betts hits three doubles and the Dodgers piled up 15 hits in a 10-4 win over the San Francisco Giants with Shohei Ohtani’s return on the horizon.
Roberts, too, has challenged De Paula to make defense a strength, one that will keep him in games, rather than lifted for a defensive replacement. And De Paula has met it with bright eyes and motivation.
“The trust on the defense is going to come,” De Paula said. “I have to prove it over time. And with the work that I’m doing on the field, I know I’m going to gain it.”
A gold glove is a goal of his too.
“That’s one thing about me, when my mind is set on something, I feel like it’s no going back,” De Paula said. “So, I’ve gotten a lot of hate on my defense, and I just love to prove people wrong. So I’m like, hey, all right, there’s a weakness there, but I’m gonna shut you up. Just give me some time. I’ve got you.”

item.title: [whittierdailynews.com] Are the Dodgers finding the best version of themselves just in time?
item.dc:creator: Doug Padilla
item.description: LOS ANGELES — The energy emanating from the steamroller heading up I-5 on Monday radiated for miles. Fuel was used to power the buses the San Diego Padres used to make the trip north for a three-game series that starts Tuesday night, but only because they didn’t try adrenaline. Winners in 13 of their past 14 games, the Padres are poised to accomplish team history over the next few days. Never in their existence have they made the playoffs in three consecutive seasons. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — The energy emanating from the steamroller heading up I-5 on Monday radiated for miles.
Fuel was used to power the buses the San Diego Padres used to make the trip north for a three-game series that starts Tuesday night, but only because they didn’t try adrenaline.
Winners in 13 of their past 14 games, the Padres are poised to accomplish team history over the next few days. Never in their existence have they made the playoffs in three consecutive seasons.
San Diego has a magic number of two to clinch a National League wild-card spot, although the Padres intend to run through the finish line with a chance at ascending to the top of the wild-card heap in the NL.
“I feel like the whole team is in a good spot right now,” San Diego’s Fernando Tatis Jr. told the San Diego Union-Tribune on Sunday. “We’re playing really good baseball. We’re checking in when we have to. The entire lineup is in a good spot right now. So when it’s going like that, it’s … a good time.”
The Dodgers already have another NL West title secured (their 13th in the past 14 years), but they also have a magic number of three to clinch a top-two seed in the NL playoffs and a bye into one of the best-of-five Division Series.
“I think it’s going to be a good kind of (playoff) primer,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of the upcoming series. “They’re a very talented team. They’re playing as good as anyone in all of baseball. I’m looking forward to playing those guys and just kind of ramping it up a little bit more for our guys.”
With the Dodgers on a 14-3 run since Sept. 3, they are on a familiar final month charge toward the playoffs. Second-half lulls in each of the past two seasons have transformed into Septembers when the group has discovered the best version of itself.
Last season, the Dodgers were swept in a three-game series by the Angels in August then opened September with a three-game dud in Pittsburgh. A disastrous loss in Baltimore lit the fire after Yoshinobu Yamamoto lost a no-hitter with two outs in the ninth inning and the Dodgers never recorded another out while losing the game.
The wide-awake Dodgers went 15-5 the rest of the way, stormed through the NL playoffs – going 9-1 against the Cincinnati Reds, Philadelphia Phillies and Milwaukee Brewers – then came out on top in a dramatic seven-game World Series against the Toronto Blue Jays.
Earlier this month, it was a brutal 8-6 loss in 10 innings to the St. Louis Cardinals on Sept. 2 that was the wake-up call. It included a four-strikeout night from Shohei Ohtani, who played just one more game before taking his current spot on the injured list.
Properly motivated, the Dodgers have gone on a tear ever since, but it has come at the expense of teams that were not in playoff contention like the Washington Nationals, Reds, Miami Marlins and San Francisco Giants.
This week marks the Dodgers’ first chance to face a team playing at the peak of its powers since they faced the Boston Red Sox, Chicago Cubs, Milwaukee Brewers and Atlanta Braves all in a recent 25-game stretch. They flubbed that test by going 1-12 in those games.
Mookie Betts, Kyle Tucker and Will Smith all have put a charge into the resurgence, while the arrival of rookie Josue De Paula has given the lineup another hitter who can extend at-bats with a discerning eye, along with Max Muncy.
Betts went 0 for 4 in Sunday’s 3-1 victory over the Giants, yet he still is hitting .373 with six home runs, 20 RBIs and a 1.215 OPS in 17 games since the start of September.
Far from content with an offense that has averaged 5.8 runs per game this month, Betts said the Dodgers can do even more. After all, Andy Pages is set to return Tuesday, while Ohtani could be back later this week.
“Some guys are hitting, some guys are not,” Betts said. “I think that’s the beauty of the lineup. You get a couple guys going, and a couple guys here can carry a team, and you never know. You just never know who’s it going to be, it’s different guys every day.”
Amid a brutal first season with the Dodgers, Tucker has done his part lately by going 15 for 36 (.417) over his past 11 games with five home runs and 11 RBIs. He was limited to coming off the bench on Sunday after he fouled a ball off his right knee on Saturday.
Tucker was not with the club for last year’s September revival, but he has helped power this one. When it comes to team potential, Tucker is a big-picture guy.
“I think our potential is winning the World Series,” Tucker said. “So (when) we do that, then I can say we reached it. But we feel like we’re in a good spot right now. Our pitching staff’s done a great job all year giving us an opportunity to win every single night. Our defense has played pretty well behind them and then offensively we’ve done a solid job as well.”
“Right now, we got a few guys that are feeling good. A few guys that are banged up. But we’re still out there grinding trying to win as many games as possible before the season ends and just trying to carry it all the way to the playoffs.”
At the very least, confidence will be high this week, in both dugouts.
UP NEXT
Padres (RHP Michael King, 12-9, 3.03 ERA) at Dodgers (TBA), Tuesday, 7:10 p.m., SportsNet LA, 570 AM

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] MLB Injury Report: Dodgers to get Shohei Ohtani, Andy Pages, and Roki Sasaki back for postseason run
item.dc:creator: Jorge Montanez
item.description: In this week's Injury Report, the Dodgers are getting a number of key players back this week as they prepare for another deep playoff run in their quest to three-peat. Alex Bregman hopes to return sometime in the postseason after suffering multiple facial fractures in a terrible, freak accident on the on-deck circle. And Dylan Cease has likely made his last start after experiencing shoulder fatigue. That and more in the final week's injury report. ⚾️ Baseball is back! MLB returns to NBC and Peac
item.content:encoded:
In this week's Injury Report, the Dodgers are getting a number of key players back this week as they prepare for another deep playoff run in their quest to three-peat. Alex Bregman hopes to return sometime in the postseason after suffering multiple facial fractures in a terrible, freak accident on the on-deck circle. And Dylan Cease has likely made his last start after experiencing shoulder fatigue. That and more in the final week's injury report.
⚾️ Baseball is back! MLB returns to NBC and Peacock in 2026! In addition to becoming the exclusive home of Sunday Night Baseball, NBC Sports will broadcast MLB Sunday Leadoff, "Opening Day" and Labor Day primetime games, the first round of the MLB Draft, the entire Wild Card round of the postseason, and much more.
Shohei Ohtani (knee, biceps)
Andy Pages (hand)
Blake Snell (groin)
Roki Sasaki (blister)
Ohtani has been out of action for the last two weeks, sidelined with lingering knee and biceps injuries. Manager Dave Roberts told reporters on Sunday that the 32-year-old star should be expected to return from the injured list and join the Dodgers lineup on Wednesday. Ohtani should be in the lineup for the remaining games to get some needed at-bats before the postseason. The team also gets Pages back this week, activating him from the injured list ahead of Tuesday's series opener against the Padres. He's been out for a month with a left hand fracture. The two additions this week are obviously a significant boost for a Dodgers team looking to three-peat. Their returns likely shift rookie Josue De Paula to a reserve or utility role.
On the pitching side, Snell left his start last Wednesday against the Reds with left groin tightness. He stated the issue was not serious and plans on making one more start before the postseason. That start isn't going to come when his spot in the rotation comes up on Tuesday, but the plan is for him to pitch over the weekend, according to Roberts.
From Yordan Alvarez to Zack Wheeler, an A-to-Z look at the players, performances, and trends that defined the 2026 MLB regular season.
Alex Bregman (face)
Bregman was struck by a foul ball while on the on-deck circle on Sunday against the Reds and was sent to the hospital, where he was diagnosed with multiple facial fractures. The freak accident is an unfortunate development this late in the season as the Cubs prepare to enter the playoffs. The team is hoping to get their 32-year-old star third baseman back at some point in the postseason, and it is a relief that the injury didn't result in anything more serious. Meanwhile, Sasaki was activated on Monday after missing some time with a blister issue and will pitch as a one-inning reliever, auditioning for a spot in the Dodgers bullpen in the postseason.
Dylan Cease (shoulder)
Cease has likely made his final start of the season. The 30-year-old right-hander underwent an MRI on his right shoulder over the weekend after experiencing some fatigue. The imaging revealed some shoulder inflammation, but no structural damage that would require surgery, and nothing that would bring into question his availability for next season. With the Blue Jays 3.5 games out of a Wild Card spot, it doesn't make much sense for Cease to push for one more start over the final weekend. If his season is indeed over, he'll end the year with a strong 2.40 ERA, 1.10 WHIP, and 239 strikeouts over 169 innings.
Andrés Muñoz (knee)
Muñoz left Sunday's game against the Rockies with a knee injury after giving up a home run and a walk. He was set to undergo an MRI on his right knee, the results of which are still unknown. The 27-year-old right-hander had a tough, disappointing season, posting a 4.24 ERA, 1.22 WHIP, and 89 strikeouts over 57 1/3 innings while converting 28 of 38 save chances. If he's unable to pitch over the final week, it could be Seranthony Domíguez closing out the remaining games.
Bryce Eldridge (concussion)
More Giants injuries that seemingly come out of nowhere. Eldridge was scratched from Friday's lineup against the Dodgers due to a head laceration after bumping his head on a low-hanging ceiling at the team hotel. He still "felt woozy" throughout the weekend and entered the concussion protocol before the team ultimately placed him on the 7-day concussion injured list. The move is retroactive to Friday, so there's a chance he could return for the final weekend series, though that's probably unlikely. The 21-year-old slugger flashed immense potential this season, hitting .269/.364/.461 with 17 homers and 57 RBI across 448 plate appearances.
Colt Keith (thumb)
Keith's season is over after the team placed him on the 10-day injured list with a left thumb sprain. It's an issue that the 25-year-old infielder has been playing through over the last several weeks. He ends the season hitting a modest .258/.322/.406 with 10 homers, 51 runs scored, 36 RBI, and six steals across 423 plate appearances.

item.title: [orlandoecho.com] Sizzling Padres can punch playoff ticket as soon as opener with Dodgers
item.description:
Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

22 Sep 2026, 03:25 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Denis Poroy)
The hottest team in baseball is racing toward a playoff berth, and the San Diego Padres can complete the chase as early as Tuesday's opener of a three-game road series against the Los Angeles Dodgers.
The Padres (87-69) have won 13 of their last 14 games to not only climb out of wild-card uncertainty but also give themselves a legitimate chance at clinching the National League's top wild-card spot over their final six regular-season games.
They can clinch a playoff spot Tuesday with a win and an Arizona Diamondbacks loss to the Colorado Rockies.
A postseason appearance would be the third consecutive for San Diego, which has never delivered a similar run in franchise history.
'This is so fun,' said Jake Cronenworth, who had two home runs and five RBIs for San Diego in its 7-3 home victory over the Miami Marlins on Sunday. 'It's hard to compare each (of the past three playoff chases). Each one's so fun in its own way and unique. But this one's been really awesome.'
Fernando Tatis Jr. added a home run, his 25th, and is batting .310 with 12 home runs and a 1.016 OPS over his past 30 games since Aug. 18.
Against their Southern California rival, the Padres are expected to send right-hander Michael King (12-9, 3.03 ERA) to the mound.
King is 4-0 with a 1.41 ERA over his last five starts and is 1-1 with a 3.12 ERA in three starts against the Dodgers this season, including an outing in May when he went seven scoreless innings. That start included a season-high nine strikeouts.
The Dodgers (96-60) also have plenty to play for after clinching the National League West title last week. They are two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers for the best record in the NL but do not hold the tiebreaker between the teams.
Los Angeles is 14-3 since Sept. 3 and has a magic number of three to clinch a top-two spot in the NL and a bye into the NL Division Series.While the Padres are on a five-game winning streak, the Dodgers have won four in a row after completing a three-game home sweep of the San Francisco Giants.
Tommy Edman hit a game-tying home run in the sixth inning for Los Angeles on Sunday, while Enrique Hernandez had a go-ahead RBI double in the seventh.
While right-hander Roki Sasaki (5-5, 4.60) is set to return from a blister issue, he will have an abbreviated outing and not necessarily as the starter. Manager Dave Roberts characterized the pitching plan as more of a bullpen game.
The Dodgers are also expected to see the return of center fielder Andy Pages for the series opener against the Padres. Pages has not played since Aug. 21 because of a broken hand.
While the Dodgers have found some success over the past three-plus weeks following a lackluster two months, their 14-3 run has not come against teams who are in playoff contention. A visit from the Padres changes that.
'I think it's going to be a good kind of primer,' Roberts said. 'They're a very talented team. They're playing as good as anyone in all of baseball. I'm looking forward to playing those guys and just kind of ramping it up a little bit more for our guys.'
--Field Level Media

item.title: [fantasy.fangraphs.com] FAAB Frenzy and Waivers Wild: Week 27
item.dc:creator: Vlad Sedler
item.description: Every Monday, this column will break down the most popular waiver wire and free agent acquisitions from the weekend. item.content:encoded:
Every Monday, this column will break down the most popular waiver wire and free agent acquisitions from the weekend. I dig into the top adds on the ever-popular Fantrax and in the NFBC Online Championship (OC), a national mid-stakes contest with 240 total leagues of 12 and a six-figure grand prize. Reviewing player adds between the two should provide us with a well-rounded perspective and barometer of the fantasy baseball marketplace.
Week 26 Overview
Hitters
The San Diego Padres took advantage of their four-game series with the Rockies at Coors Field and a home set with the Marlins, scoring 51 runs, 12 more than any other team. Fernando Tatis Jr. (along with Brandon Lowe and Pete Crow-Armstrong) led the way with a week-high four dingers. Last week’s streamers turned out to be dynamite: Jake Cronenworth (.464-8-2-8-2), Dustin Harris (.379-5-0-7-2) and Samad Taylor (.556-6-1-7-1) really stepped up, particularly Taylor for my competitive Main Event squad that gained two category points in batting average last week. Rake Cronenworth was true to his nickname from several years ago. He led all Major League hitters with 13 hits. The Brewers swiped a league-high 12 bags last week: four each for Jackson Chourio and rookie Cooper Pratt. Tampa’s Chandler Simpson led all runners with five swipes, finally catching Washington’s Nasim Nuñez for the MLB lead with 46. Expect Simpson to finish with 50+ and win the stolen base crown.
Pitchers
Of the 29 two-start pitchers excluding Pirates opener Lake Bachar, three earned two wins: Tarik Skubal, Sean Burke and David Peterson. Houston’s Hunter Brown had an outstanding two-step (10 IP – 5 H – 1 ER – 5 K – 20 K) and those 20 punchouts led all pitchers for the week. Gavin Williams punched out 16 in 12 innings and is back atop the AL lead in strikeouts with 244. Dylan Cease (239) may not make his final start of the season and Cam Schlittler (234) is unlikely to catch Williams as both have one start remaining. It’s very possible that Williams catches and passes Jacob Misiorowski (247) for the Major League lead. The Miz pitched three innings in his weekend start and might be limited for his final one.
Tampa’s Bryan Baker was the first reliever to reach 40 saves this season. It’s possible that Cade Smith (39), Riley O’Brien (38) and Mason Miller (37) join Baker. The last time there were three closers with 40 or more saves was in 2019: Edwin Díaz (57), Wade Davis (43), and Craig Kimbrel (42). Shout out to folks who drafted O’Brien late, and/or picked up Baker, Louis Varland or Jacob Latz off waivers and didn’t have to worry about the saves category all season.
Week 27 Most Added Players: NFBC Main Event, NFBC OC, and Fantrax
It’s the last hurrah for managers with FAB dollars left, hoping to get the best bang for the buck and for variance to lean their way and tip them into league titles. As is usually the case in the final week, we hope to optimize our pitching rotations and hitters in hitter-friendly ballparks against bad pitching. It was odd seeing Shohei Ohtani available in several leagues, and perhaps fortuitous as he should be activated this week and start a few games. Ohtani was acquired in 26 OCs for an AWB of $17. In Main Events, there were 12 shares available and they went for a reasonable $12 a pop. I scooped up a rare Ohtani share in an OC for $2, winning a tiebreaker over the team in 1st place in that league. Andy Pages will be activated on Tuesday, which should push Tommy Edman back to second base. Pages had been out since August 21, but was producing at an exciting clip before the injury — .272 – 72 R – 21 HR – 80 RBI – 12 SB in 550 PA. Managers who acquired him are hoping that he dusts the cobwebs back off and gets right into the swing of things, with all the marbles on the line.
| # | Player | Team | Position(s) | % of Lgs Added | AWB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Andy Pages | LAD | OF | 60% | $5 |
| 2 | JR Ritchie | ATL | SP | 57% | $3 |
| 3 | Daniel Lynch IV | KC | SP | 57% | $6 |
| 4 | Samad Taylor | SD | OF | 48% | $5 |
| 5 | Jose Siri | LAA | OF | 45% | $4 |
| 6 | Heliot Ramos | NYY | OF | 35% | $7 |
| 7 | Dansby Swanson | CHC | SS | 35% | $8 |
| 8 | Brayan Bello | BOS | SP | 35% | $11 |
| 9 | Dustin Harris | SD | OF | 32% | $10 |
| 10 | Garrett Whitlock | BOS | RP | 32% | $5 |
| 11 | Pavin Smith | ARI | 1B | 30% | $4 |
| 12 | Anthony Volpe | NYY | SS | 30% | $5 |
AWB = Average Winning Bid (min: $4 AWB)
Pitchers were the most popular targets, specifically two-steppers, as we chase wins and strikeouts, hoping the Ratio Monster doesn’t eat our leads in ERA and WHIP. JR Ritchie and Daniel Lynch IV were the most added starters who we expect two starts from this week. Ritchie’s MLB debut back in April came with great promise, but walks haunted him greatly, which led to trips back to Triple-A to refine his craft and some bulk inning relief work when he returned to Atlanta in July. Ritchie was recently promoted again, and ran into a juggernaut Cubs offense last week, allowing six runs on seven hits in 4.2 innings. The walk rate (13.7%) isn’t pretty, and he has a good opportunity to end his season on a high note with two reasonable matchups — against the Reds at home and the Marlins on the road. Lynch had served the Royals well as their top southpaw out of the bullpen for most of the season. He moved to the rotation in August and slowly worked his pitch counts upward. Lynch has made it to five innings in each of his last three starts. His latest one (at HOU on September 16) went well — 5 IP – 2 H – 0 ER – 1 BB – 3 K. More of that please as he faces the White Sox and Guardians at Kauffman Stadium in the final week. If I could only choose one for the week, it would be Ritchie.
Red Sox pitchers Brayan Bello and Garrett Whitlock were popular buys as the likelihood of roto stars shining bright on them this week is high. Bello is coming off a tremendous outing against the AL-leading Rays on Saturday where he posted an 11:0 K:BB with just one run allowed in eight innings. Those 11 punchies tied his career high. Bello had been the worst starter in the game (6.49 ERA, 1.67 WHIP) through June 4, when he was optioned to Triple-A. Since the All-Star break, mostly out of relief and with two starts, the 27-year-old has been shining. Over those 51.1 innings, he is rocking exemplary ratios (2.28 ERA, 1.01 WHIP) and a 17% K-BB% (22.3% K, 5.3% BB). Bello should make a start against the Cubs next Saturday. The Cubs should be settled into a playoff spot by then, so perhaps they give Pete Crow-Armstrong and some of the other regulars that day off. Boston’s closer Aroldis Chapman has been day-to-day with a lat issue, so perhaps the Red sox have him take it easy and provide Whitlock with some save opportunities. Whitlock has a 7-2 record with a 17.5 ERA, 0.88 WHIP and four saves.
Streaming Diamondbacks is a good idea this week, specifically for their three-game set at Coors Field against the Rockies in the early part of the week. Pavin Smith was a coveted target, coming off a four-day stretch where three of his hits were home runs. Don’t expect Smith to start against lefty Kyle Freeland, but he should be in the lineup for the other two contests against righties. Nolan Arenado was available in one of the 60 Main Event leagues and was acquired for just one dollar.
Better late than never for two punchless Padres who have been quite productive and certainly enjoyed their visit to Coors Field in the first half of last week. Dustin Harris ($10 AWB) and Samad Taylor ($5) have been red hot and playing often over the last 10 days. Though he doesn’t have a home run yet, Harris has been quite productive and helpful to early-bird managers: eight runs, 12 runs batted in and three steals, batting .384 with a 166 wRC+ in 40 plate appearances since September 11. He’s also been batting second against right-handed starters. Taylor has at least one hit in nine of his last 10, including a 3-for-3 effort on Sunday, and has driven in seven in his last seven games.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Dustin Harris | SD | OF | 34% | $8 |
| 2 | Cristian Javier | HOU | SP | 33% | $7 |
| 3 | Anthony Kay | CHW | SP | 24% | $10 |
| 4 | Robert Gasser | MIL | SP | 22% | $9 |
| 5 | Daniel Lynch IV | KC | SP | 22% | $7 |
| 6 | Jonah Cox | SF | OF | 22% | $8 |
| 7 | Josh Jung | TEX | 3B | 21% | $6 |
| 8 | Yusei Kikuchi | LAA | SP | 20% | $4 |

| 12 | Andrew Alvarez | WAS | SP | 16% | $8 |
| 13 | JR Ritchie | ATL | SP | 15% | $5 |
AWB = Average Winning Bid (min: $4 AWB)
As always, more reliable starting pitcher depth was available in the 12-team OC pool. Cristian Javier, Anthony Kay, Robert Gasser, Lynch, Yusei Kikuchi, and Max Scherzer were the most added pitchers this week. Javier should pitch twice this week and will hope to put his best foot forward (in this case, his right arm) as the Astros fight for the AL West and a playoff spot. Sutter Health Park is not a fun place to pitch, but the A’s lineup is a watered-down version without Brent Rooker, Nick Kurtz, Tyler Soderstrom, and Jacob Wilson윌슨. Javier’s first start is in Seattle may not be a picnic with gluten-free granola and Pearl Jam on the Discman.
Milwaukee’s Robert Gasser only draws one start (home vs. STL), but is considered a reliable ratios guy who can score a much-needed win for fantasy managers, as the Brewers will certainly be favorites in that matchup. Gasser earned his fifth win on Saturday, throwing seven scoreless innings against the Orioles. White Sox lefty Anthony Kay has good matchups (at KC on Tuesday and vs. COL on Sunday), though that second start could be pulled away from him. The main problems here is that Kay hasn’t made it to the fifth inning in any of his last five starts. I feel much more comfortable with a single start against the Orioles from Max Scherzer than I do a double (at SEA, at ATH) from wily Yusei Kikuchi. Kikuchi has walked 12 batters in his last three starts.
| # | Player | Team | Position | Roster % | +/- |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Ryan Johnson | LAA | SP | 50% | 12% |
| 2 | Dustin Harris | SD | OF | 18% | 10% |
| 3 | Jack Perkins | ATH | RP | 26% | 7% |
| 4 | Dean Kremer | MIN | SP | 45% | 7% |
| 5 | Ryan Watson | LAA | RP | 10% | 6% |
| 6 | Andrew Alvarez | WSH | SP | 46% | 6% |
| 7 | David Peterson | CHC | SP | 56% | 5% |
| 8 | David Sandlin | CHW | RP | 21% | 5% |
| 9 | Victor Mesa Jr. | TB | OF | 43% | 4% |
| 10 | Leo Bernal | STL | C | 35% | 3% |
| 11 | Javier Sanoja | MIA | 2B,3B,SS,OF | 62% | 3% |
(+/-) is the % of leagues the player was added to in the previous week
It’s possible that attraction towards Ryan Johnson this weekend relates to dynasty and keeper formats, and not his start in Seattle this week. Johnson has limited run damage over his last nine starts, since August 6, posting a 2.39 ERA, but with an xFIP (5.01) nearly double the mark. Johnson is more of a 4.25-4.50 ERA guy than a sub-3.00 ERA one, as his 90.9% LOB and .229 BABIP portends.
Perhaps a similar mindset applies to folks who scooped up Jack Perkins, who pitched two quality starts on the road against the Rays (6.2 IP – 4 H – 0 ER – 1 BB – 8 K) and the Guardians (6 IP – 5 H – 1 ER – 0 BB – 4 K), flashing some of his upside and future potential. Perkins has had a difficult season (5.90 ERA, but a 4.16 xFIP, 1.45 WHIP) and will be a tough streamer at home in Sacramento next season, but the strikeouts (25.2%) should always be there.
Andrew Alvarez should have a rotation spot with the Nationals next season. He has been outstanding since the All-Star break, posting a 2.44 ERA (3.30 FIP, 4.02 xFIP) with a 1.10 WHIP and a 22.7% strikeout rate, though he wasn’t able to secure a win in any of those 10 starts. Alvarez won’t be a particularly coveted target in drafts next season, but should have a NFBC ADP somewhere in the 250-325 overall range. He may be a consideration in NL-only keeper leagues with deep benches and five-plus keepers.
Bold Predictions for Week 27
Gavin Williams and Jacob Misiorowski finish the season tied for the MLB lead in strikeouts with 255. Williams punches out 11 and Misiorowski, eight.
JR Ritchie steps up for his two starts and has a Jack Perkins Week 26 type week, helping managers win league titles.
Cade Cavalli twirls a gem in Detroit this week and pulls his 3.02 ERA under 3.00 to end the season. Cavalli will have a top-60 ADP in 2027.
Jo Adell takes advantage of four left-handed starters this week and earns seven RBIs to reach 100, after falling two RBIs short last season.
One of Cristian Javier or Yusei Kikuchi will remind why streaming pitchers in Sutter Health Park, even if part of a two-step, is a mistake.
Miguel Vargas and Colson Montgomery hit three home runs each this week and the White Sox score the most runs in Week 27.
The Houston Astros win the NL West and knock the Texas Rangers out of playoff contention.
I hope you enjoyed my column this season and that you found it helpful, or at least entertaining and informative. Stay tuned for more from me next week as we hit the offseason streets. Best of luck this final week!
Vlad writes for RotoGraphs and is the head of fantasy baseball content at FTN Fantasy. He is a Tout Wars Expert League champ, member of the CDM Fantasy Sports Hall of Fame and has been nominated for FSWA writing awards six times. Vlad has been playing fantasy baseball since 1995, winning 42 NFBC leagues since 2012 and ranking in the top percentile in NFBC’s Online Championship contest (33% win rate, 52% cash rate; 64 leagues). Much to the chagrin of his colleagues and most baseball aficionados, Vlad is a lifelong Dodgers fan who claims his first gut call at age 9 was Kirk Gibson’s 1988 World Series home run. You can follow him on X and BlueSky @RotoGut.

item.title: [thebiglead.com] Dodgers activate two key players immediately before big Padres series
item.dc:creator: J P Hoornstra
item.description: With one week left in the MLB regular season, the Los Angeles Dodgers are getting two key players back for a three-game home series against the San Diego Padres. Pitcher Roki Sasaki and center fielder Andy Pages, who have been on the injured list since August, were activated from it on Monday, an off day for the Dodgers and Padres. item.content:encoded:
With one week left in the MLB regular season, the Los Angeles Dodgers are getting two key players back for a three-game home series against the San Diego Padres.
Pitcher Roki Sasaki and center fielder Andy Pages, who have been on the injured list since August, were activated from it on Monday, an off day for the Dodgers and Padres. The two National League West rivals can each clinch something important at Dodger Stadium—a berth in the postseason for San Diego and a first-round bye for Los Angeles.
Sasaki posted a 3.05 ERA in seven starts after the All-Star break but developed a blister on his throwing hand in August. Pages played in his first All-Star Game in July but fractured a bone in his right hand when he was hit by a 100.2 mph fastball from Pittsburgh Pirates starter Bubba Chandler on Aug. 21.
The Dodgers were able to clinch the National League West without the two players, but both figure to play key roles in October for the defending World Series champions.
Postseason roles
The team lost hard-throwing reliever Edgardo Henriquez to a back injury earlier this month. For all his second-half success as a starter, the Dodgers need Sasaki more in their bullpen as a right-handed complement to left-handers Tanner Scott and Alex Vesia.
Pages, meanwhile, was excelling at the plate and in the field prior to his injury, which required surgery. He’ll have six games to tune up for the postseason—and a chance at redemption for last October.
The Dodgers won the World Series even though Pages had only four hits in 16 postseason games, managing just an .078 batting average across four playoff rounds.
Without Pages, the Dodgers moved veteran utilityman Tommy Edman to center field. Through week’s end, he was slashing .245/.328/.376 (94 OPS+) in 79 games this season.
The Dodgers are also expecting Shohei Ohtani to return during the Padres series, but he isn’t eligible to be activated from the 15-day injured list before Wednesday.
In corresponding 26-man roster moves, pitcher Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliezer Alfonzo were optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers playoff roster projection: Could Edwin Díaz, Josue De Paula, even Hyeseong Kim surprise?

item.content:encoded:
Entering the final week of the regular season, the Dodgers more or less know their postseason fate.
They've locked up the National League West. They are a seemingly safe four games clear of the Atlanta Braves for a first-round bye. And, unless they can close a two-game gap on the Milwaukee Brewers without holding the tiebreaker, they will finish as the NL's No. 2 seed, getting home-field advantage at least for the NL Division Series.
Thus, the real intrigue for now is who might be on the Dodgers' postseason roster when the playoffs begin next month.
This year, injuries and fluctuating performances have forced them to cycle 53 different players through their clubhouse.
And while the core of the group is clear, many questions remain about how the club will construct its lineup and pitching staff for this fall's pursuit of a third-straight World Series.
Here is the California Post's best guess about how it will all shake out.
Lineup locks
Will Smith, Freddie Freeman, Tommy Edman, Mookie Betts, Max Muncy, Teoscar Hernández, Andy Pages, Kyle Tucker, Shohei Ohtani, Kiké Hernández, Miguel Rojas, Hunter Feduccia
There won't be any big surprises in how the Dodgers line up to begin the playoffs, assuming Ohtani is healthy enough to resume everyday DH'ing duties.
Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker have cemented their place as everyday hitters thanks to late-season surges. Andy Pages is due back on Tuesday from a fractured hand. Freddie Freeman still seems somewhat limited by his right knee injury, but has nonetheless been able to manage it well enough to this point. And while Tommy Edman has been slumping lately, he doesn't seem to be in immediate danger of losing at-bats.
On the bench, Hunter Feduccia has locked up the back-up catching job, and could be a left-handed hitting option as a pinch-hitter. Kiké Hernández and Miguel Rojas, meanwhile, each provide versatile defensive depth, as well as extensive track records for postseason heroics when called upon.
Entering the final week of the regular season, the core of the Dodgers' position player group looks as they expected.
Dodgers Lineup questions
Bubble candidates: Josue De Paula, Dalton Rushing, Alex Call, Alex Freeland, Hyeseong Kim
The Dodgers will still have one, if not two, position player spots to fill depending on how they construct their roster (i.e. an even 13 pitchers/13 hitters, or a 12/14 split like they used last year?)
And for those, they could have a number of difficult decisions.
First and foremost: Will Josue De Paula make the playoff roster?
If he does, it will likely be as a left-handed bench bat; though if there is any lingering uncertainty with Ohtani, he could also provide insurance as a backup DH option. His main competition right now figures to be Alex Call (who might be redundant to Rojas and Hernández as a right-handed bench bat) or Dalton Rushing (who is an intriguing alternative as a left-handed bat, but remains sidelined from the setback he suffered with his elbow injury earlier this month).
In just 10 MLB games, De Paula has quickly built a strong case, showing supreme plate discipline (10 walks to only four strikeouts) and the potential for power (three doubles, one home run, seven RBIs). At this point, it might be more of a surprise if he doesn't make it.
If the Dodgers elect to carry an extra position player on top of that, the choices are even more varied.
Last year, they rostered two base-running/defensive specialists throughout the playoffs in infielder Hyeseong Kim and outfielder Justin Dean. Dean is now gone, and Hernández could serve as a late-game defensive outfield replacement anyway. But Kim remains in consideration, manager Dave Roberts said, thanks to his speed and infield glove. Alex Freeland could also factor in here, as someone capable of providing more at the plate.
Lineup projection for Los Angeles
C: Will Smith
1B: Freddie Freeman
2B: Tommy Edman
SS: Mookie Betts
3B: Max Muncy
LF: Teoscar Hernández
CF: Andy Pages
RF: Kyle Tucker
DH: Shohei Ohtani
Bench: Kiké Hernández, Miguel Rojas, Hunter Feduccia, Josue De Paula, Hyeseong Kim*
*If the Dodgers carry 14 position players
Dodgers pitching staff locks
Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow, Roki Sasaki, Tanner Scott, Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips
The Dodgers' starting rotation is set, assuming no further setbacks with Blake Snell's groin injury. The back end of the bullpen has come into focus, too, with Tanner Scott and/or Roki Sasaki the most logical candidates to serve as closer, and Alex Vesia and Evan Phillips separating themselves as the team's next most-trusted high-leverage relief options.
The only real question here is how the Dodgers will line up the rotation. Yamamoto-Skubal would make sense for Games 1 and 2 of a division series (keeping them both on-line for a potential Game 5). But could Tyler Glasnow's potential issues with traveling tempt the Dodgers to use him primarily at home, if they can? All factors to consider in the coming weeks.
Pitching staff questions
Roster bubble candidates: Brock Stewart, Edwin Díaz, Blake Treinen, Kris Bubic, Jack Dreyer, Emmet Sheehan, Justin Wrobleski, Edgardo Henriquez, Will Klein, Eric Lauer
The first thing the Dodgers need to figure out here is health.
Edgardo Henriquez will almost certainly be on the playoff roster, and pitching in a high-leverage role, if he can make a full recovery from his recent back strain. Will Klein and Eric Lauer might also be available health-wise, though lack clear roles to step immediately back into.
Otherwise, the Dodgers will effectively have at least four open spots for six to seven other pitchers.
For added right-handed depth, they might be deciding between Brock Stewart (who has been a go-to weapon against right-handed hitters recently), Edwin Díaz (who is trying to salvage his dismal debut season, and did throw a pair of scoreless outings this weekend) and Blake Treinen (who has curiously pitched only five times in three weeks since being activated from the injured list, and not in the highest of leverage).
For another left-handed option, they could go with Kris Bubic (the trade deadline acquisition who has impressed with three scoreless appearances since returning from an injury) or Jack Dreyer (who was one of the Dodgers' best relievers from June to August, but has given up five runs in his last seven outings).
And for a multi-inning role, they will have Emmet Sheehan (who has looked like a different pitcher in three sterling starts since returning from a minor-league demotion) and Justin Wrobleski (the breakout All-Star who has finally shaken some of his home run problems since moving to the bullpen).
There are many permutations that the Dodgers could employ depending on opponent. They're still figuring out the exact hierarchy of all their bullpen arms, too.
But as long as their rotation is dominant, everything else should take care of itself.
Pitching staff projection
Rotation: Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow
Bullpen: Roki Sasaki, Tanner Scott, Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips, Brock Stewart, Kris Bubic, Edwin Díaz, Emmet Sheehan, Justin Wrobleski

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers have lineup problem they cannot afford to solve by benching Josue De Paula
item.dc:creator: Miracle Dimwesh
item.description: Josue De Paula was supposed to give the Los Angeles Dodgers another young bat for the final weeks of the regular season. Instead, the rookie has created a lineup problem the team may not be able to ignore. De Paula has been too productive to simply remove from the lineup. The 21-year-old has reached base at a .474 clip through his first 10 MLB games, giving the Dodgers another dangerous left-handed hitter before the postseason. item.content:encoded:
Josue De Paula was supposed to give the Los Angeles Dodgers another young bat for the final weeks of the regular season. Instead, the rookie has created a lineup problem the team may not be able to ignore.
De Paula has been too productive to simply remove from the lineup. The 21-year-old has reached base at a .474 clip through his first 10 MLB games, giving the Dodgers another dangerous left-handed hitter before the postseason.
That creates an interesting problem when Shohei Ohtani returns. The Dodgers have several established outfielders, but De Paula's bat is making it harder to find room for everyone.
Josue De Paula has been doing this all year
The rookie's hot start is not coming out of nowhere. De Paula dominated Double-A pitching throughout the season before earning his September call-up.
Minor League Baseball named him the 2026 Texas League MVP on Monday. He hit .303/.401/.547 with 27 home runs, 31 stolen bases, 152 hits and 104 RBIs in 124 games for Tulsa.
That production earned him a direct jump from Double-A to Los Angeles. He has continued showing the same offensive approach against MLB pitching.
De Paula has gone 8-for-28 with 10 walks, one home run and seven RBIs in his first 10 games. He has also played two games in left field, showing the Dodgers can move him around when necessary.
Dodgers face a difficult Ohtani lineup decision
Feb 24, 2026; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Josue De Paula against the Cleveland Guardians during a spring training game at Camelback Ranch-Glendale. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
The situation becomes more complicated with Ohtani nearing a return. Manager Dave Roberts said there is a good chance Ohtani will be activated Wednesday against the San Diego Padres. He will return as a hitter, not a pitcher.
That puts Ohtani back at DH and removes the easiest path to keeping De Paula in the lineup.
The Dodgers already have Kyle Tucker in right field, Teoscar Hernández in left and Andy Pages in center. Tucker signed a four-year, $240 million deal before the season, while Hernández and Pages have remained important parts of the club's outfield plans.
De Paula can play the outfield, but moving him there would force another decision. Taking one of the established outfielders out also means changing a group that has helped Los Angeles reach this point.
The Dodgers do not have to solve the entire problem today. But De Paula's performance has made one thing clear: when Ohtani returns, finding enough at-bats for everyone will be one of Dave Roberts' biggest lineup challenges heading into October.

item.content:encoded:
We’ve made it to the final week of the regular season. There are still two divisions in the American League up for grabs, a couple of long-shot playoff hopefuls looking to make a last-minute run, and playoff seeding to fight over. It should make for a dramatic end to a great season.
Our power rankings use a modified Elo rating system. If you’re familiar with chess rankings, you’ll know that Elo is an elegant ranking format that measures teams’ relative strength and is very reactive to recent performance. To avoid overweighting recent results during the season, we weigh each team’s raw Elo rank using our coin flip playoff odds (specifically, we regress the playoff odds by 50% and weigh those against the raw Elo ranking, increasing in weight as the season progresses to a maximum of 25%). The weighted Elo ranks are then displayed as “Power Score” in the tables below. As the best and worst teams sort themselves out between now and October, they’ll filter to the top and bottom of the rankings, while the exercise remains reactive to hot streaks and cold snaps. If you’re looking for a visual representation of the ups and downs of your team throughout the season, look no further than the brand new Power Rankings Board in the FanGraphs Lab.
First up are the full rankings, presented in a sortable table. Below that, I’ve grouped the teams into tiers with comments on a handful of clubs. You’ll notice that the official ordinal rankings don’t always match the tiers — there are times where I take editorial liberties when grouping teams together — but generally, the ordering is consistent. One thing to note: The playoff odds listed in the tables below are our standard Depth Charts odds, not the coin flip odds that are used in the ranking formula.

It was a great week for the Brewers. They won their fourth straight NL Central title and sixth in the last nine years, and also set another franchise record for wins in a single season, one year after setting the previous record. They now have a chance to win 100 games for the first time in club history this week and still have the top seed in the NL to play for.
The Rays swept the Athletics and won their series against the Red Sox last week to put some distance between themselves and the Yankees in the AL East race. The gap in the division is now six games, and even though the two rivals play each other four times during the final week of the season, it would take a massive collapse from Tampa Bay to upset the current standings. Because the Rays also currently lead the season series with the Yankees, 6-3, all they need is to win one of the four games in New York to take the division title. With Shane McClanahan still recovering from his forearm injury — his availability for the playoffs is up in the air — Freddy Peralta has stepped up to lead the pitching staff over the last few weeks. Across his last five starts, he’s allowed just three runs in 28 2/3 innings. That’s the kind of production the Rays were hoping to get when they acquired him at the trade deadline.
| Team | Record | Elo | Opponent Elo | Playoff Odds | Power Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dodgers | 96-60 | 1580 | 1492 | 100.0% | 1621 |
| Padres | 87-69 | 1578 | 1501 | 97.2% | 1618 |
| Braves | 92-64 | 1565 | 1500 | 100.0% | 1610 |
| Yankees | 89-66 | 1556 | 1497 | 100.0% | 1603 |
The Dodgers are getting all their pieces in place for the postseason. Andy Pages and Roki Sasaki will be activated off the IL on Tuesday, and Shohei Ohtani should follow on Wednesday. There’s a lingering question about Blake Snell’s status after he injured his groin last week, but it sounds like he’ll be able to make a start during the final weekend of the season. And even though the majority of the year has been a slog for Kyle Tucker, his bat seems to have finally woken up at the right time; he collected nine hits and three home runs last week.
Having won 13 of their last 14 games, the Padres are peaking at exactly the right moment. They’ve surged five games ahead of the Diamondbacks and one ahead of the Phillies in the NL Wild Card standings, and are now tied with the Cubs for the top spot. San Diego’s final series of the season against Arizona still looms large, especially if the Friars stumble against the Dodgers in the series beforehand. You’re probably familiar with Fernando Tatis Jr.’s hot streak — he blasted four home runs last week to bring his total in September up to eight — but the biggest contributor to the Padres’ success recently has been Ty France. He had 12 hits and a home run last week and has posted a fantastic 168 wRC+ during the second half of the season.
After a couple of years away from the top, the Braves are NL East champions again — it’s their seventh division title in the last nine years. Atlanta’s dominance this year has been a welcome return to form. Even though his season has been a bit up and down, Ronald Acuña Jr. is looking like the superstar that won the MVP back in 2023 again. Last week, he smacked three home runs, including a go-ahead grand slam on Saturday, and is running a 191 wRC+ in September.
A little more than a week after being activated off the IL, Aaron Judge is back on the shelf, this time with a calf injury sustained on Wednesday. His availability for the playoffs is still up in the air, though he’s confident that he’ll be able to return sooner rather than later. Thankfully, Jazz Chisholm Jr. should be activated off the IL on Tuesday, and there’s some confidence that Trent Grisham will also be ready to return for the postseason. It helps that Ben Rice has bounced back from a rough August to post a 192 wRC+ in September. Still, Judge’s injury is a major blow to the Yankees’ hopes for a deep October run.
| Team | Record | Elo | Opponent Elo | Playoff Odds | Power Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Red Sox | 84-72 | 1544 | 1500 | 100.0% | 1594 |
| Phillies | 86-70 | 1546 | 1501 | 97.3% | 1593 |
| Cubs | 87-69 | 1539 | 1501 | 99.9% | 1590 |
Even though the Red Sox lost both of their series last week, they managed to clinch a postseason berth on Sunday. It’s the cap to a remarkable turnaround after the team looked completely lost in mid-June. Boston can officially secure the second Wild Card spot with a couple of wins against the Guardians this week. Then the team can turn its attention to the Yankees and the rematch of last year’s Wild Card matchup between these two historic rivals.
Nothing is going to come easy for the Phillies over the next few weeks. The team placed Jesús Luzardo on the IL last week with a shoulder injury, but thankfully, it sounds like he’ll be ready to pitch in the playoffs. But before they count their chickens, they need to actually clinch a playoff spot. Philadelphia is four games up on the Diamondbacks in the NL Wild Card race, but its upcoming opponents are no cake walk; the Phillies have the Brewers and Rays on the schedule to finish off the regular season. Facing two of the best teams in baseball is quite a test ahead of the postseason, and the Phillies haven’t exactly been playing well lately.
The biggest concern for the Cubs right now is the status of Alex Bregman. He was struck by a foul ball in the face while standing in the on-deck circle during Sunday’s game and was taken to the hospital for further evaluation. Alongside Pete Crow-Armstrong, Bregman has been one of the best hitters in baseball since the All-Star break. It would be a huge blow if the third baseman had to miss any significant amount of time at this point in the season. As for Crow-Armstrong, he’s two stolen bases away from joining the 40/40 club. He put a few finishing touches on his MVP case last week by bopping four more home runs, bringing his season total up to 45.
| Team | Record | Elo | Opponent Elo | Playoff Odds | Power Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Guardians | 81-75 | 1520 | 1498 | 97.6% | 1572 |

There was some upheaval in the two division races represented in this tier. Entering last week one game behind the White Sox in the AL Central standings, the Guardians took two of three games against the South Siders in a dramatic series, which included a walk-off on Tuesday and an improbable go-ahead homer on Wednesday. From there, although Chicago took advantage of playing — and winning — on Thursday while Cleveland was off to pull back into a tie atop the division, the Guardians just kept winning, sweeping the the Athletics over the weekend to bring their winning streak to five. José Ramírez finally broke out of his extended slump, tallying nine hits, a home run, and four stolen bases last week.
As for the White Sox, they won three of their four games against the the Tigers, but that one loss was enough to drop them to a game behind Cleveland in the Central. Still, the Sox have a three-game cushion for the final AL Wild Card spot, and they own the tiebreaker over the Guardians, meaning both first place and a potential first-round bye are still in their sights. Miguel Vargas is carrying most of the load for the lineup right now, hitting three home runs last week, but he needs some support if Chicago wants to make some noise in the postseason.
Over in the AL West, the Astros were swept by the Braves this past weekend, allowing the Rangers to jump into first place with a .500 record. Texas enters this week one game up, but crucially Houston holds the tiebreaker. If the Rangers can manage to hang on, it would be just their second postseason appearance in the last decade. The last time they made the playoffs, they won the World Series.
The Houston bullpen was responsible for the backbreaking losses on Saturday and Sunday, but the lack of offense has been a much bigger problem. Over the Astros’ last 10 games, they’ve scored more than four runs in a game just once. Yordan Alvarez looked fine last week (eight hits, including two home runs) after his ankle scare the previous weekend, and Jeremy Peña has been great too (10 hits, three homers), but the rest of the lineup has been struggling. During this 10-game stretch, Houston hitters not named Alvarez or Peña have combined for an ugly 55 wRC+.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

The Diamondbacks managed to keep their slim playoff hopes alive with a pair of wins over the Yankees on Saturday and Sunday. The first victory was a walk-off and the second was highlighted by a go-ahead grand slam from Nolan Arenado. Arizona needs to take care of business in Colorado and get some help from the Dodgers to ensure that the final series against the Padres has some stakes. There’s a chance the Phillies could crash out, opening another window for the Snakes, but the direct path is through San Diego.
The Blue Jays’ hopes for a last-minute surge into the playoffs were dashed last week when they lost both of their series to the Tigers and Rangers. They’re three games back and have the Astros to contend with if they want to try and sneak into that final Wild Card spot. It’s probably too little, too late, but the team is activating Trey Yesavage off the IL on Monday as one more reinforcement ahead of a final push.

The series between the Orioles and Mets last week in Queens turned out to be more interesting than you’d expect from two teams mired in hugely disappointing seasons. Pete Alonso made his first appearance as a member of the opposing team at Citi Field and wound up hitting his 300th career home run on Tuesday, a game-tying shot in the ninth inning. He received a huge ovation from the hometown crowd, which drew some irksome comments from a few Mets players and staff after the game. Baltimore wound up sweeping New York to cut its deficit in the AL Wild Card race to 2.5 games. Alas, a sweep by the Brewers over the weekend slammed the door shut on any playoff hopes the O’s still had.
Even though the Marlins’ season essentially ended with that 12-game losing streak back in July, they have made some significant progress in their quest to become a contending club. Otto Lopez looks like a star they can build the lineup around, while Eury Pérez and Max Meyer should be strong enough to anchor the pitching staff in the years ahead. There’s also a cohort of young prospects in the upper minors who should be making their debuts soon. The future in Miami is brighter than it’s been in a while.
This is the huge step forward the Reds were hoping to see from Elly De La Cruz. In September, he has blasted seven home runs, including in five straight games earlier this month, and is running a major league-best 236 wRC+. It’s too bad the rest of Cincinnati’s roster is a bit of a mess. Sal Stewart has been excellent as De La Cruz’s sidekick, but the starting rotation has struggled mightily, and the big injury to Hunter Greene has thrown the ceiling of that group up in the air heading into next year. Still, building around a superstar like De La Cruz should make things easier if the resources to improve the rest of the roster are made available.

The AL Central crown runs through Kansas City; both the White Sox and Guardians travel to face the Royals during the final week of the season. Unfortunately, the Royals haven’t been playing well enough recently to act as a spoiler. They ended August with a 13-3 stretch, but they’ve been the worst team in the AL in September, with just five wins in 18 games.
It took a lot longer than expected, but the Twins were finally eliminated from the playoff race last week. It was a drama-filled week, too. They won a wild extra-inning walk-off affair against the Yankees on Wednesday and then were walked-off twice against the Angels between two shutout victories over the weekend. Even though they all made their big league debuts over the last few weeks, Walker Jenkins, Kaelen Culpepper, and Emmanuel Rodriguez never all appeared in a game together. That trio represents the future of the organization, so it’s a little disappointing that that future couldn’t be realized in a small way this year.

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Dodgers have high expectations but cautious plan for Andy Pages
item.dc:creator: Matt Borelli
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are set to welcome back several key contributors this week, with Andy Pages expected to return for Tuesday’s series opener against the San Diego Padres. Pages won’t go on a Minor League rehab assignment before rejoining the Dodgers because of how late it is in the season, so he has six games to prepare for the playoffs. While live at-bats will be important to help him get back to game speed, the team plans to be cautious with his immediate workload. “So we have obviously,
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are set to welcome back several key contributors this week, with Andy Pages expected to return for Tuesday’s series opener against the San Diego Padres.
Pages won’t go on a Minor League rehab assignment before rejoining the Dodgers because of how late it is in the season, so he has six games to prepare for the playoffs. While live at-bats will be important to help him get back to game speed, the team plans to be cautious with his immediate workload.
“So we have obviously, assuming he gets back on Tuesday, then there’s six in a row, and that seems pretty aggressive,” manager Dave Roberts explained.
“So I think that we do want to get him as many at-bats as possible, but we have to make sure that his legs are under him, feeling good, so we don’t go backward or get injured in that respect. So it is going to be a balancing act, and just keeping a keen eye on Andy for sure.”
Pages has been on the 10-day injured list since Aug. 22 due to a left hand fracture. He underwent a procedure that involved inserting a screw into his left hand to accelerate the recovery process without extending the recovery timeline.
Pages was in the midst of a career year prior to landing on the IL and consistently put together quality at-bats for the Dodgers. Roberts expects more of the same when the 25-year-old returns, even if he initially gets off to a slow start following the long layoff.
“Yeah, I think I’m expecting good at-bats,” Roberts said. “I can’t speak to the performance. I think I just want him to have good at-bats. I’m not sure where he’s going to hit, somewhere in middle to the bottom, I think for me. But yeah, I don’t know. I think I’m waiting just like you guys are waiting to see how it looks.”
Pages provides even more value to the Dodgers with his elite defense in center field. Even in the event he struggles at the plate, Roberts believes he has a higher floor than most players because of his arm and glove.
“The defense is a big reason why he’s still a valuable player, even coming off the IL with the uncertainty of the offense, which we’ll still bet on. But playing at premium position and playing it well is hugely important,” Roberts said.
Andy Pages’ unique recovery
Pages first began hitting off a tee before progressing to swings off a pitching machine. More recently, he logged at-bats against the Trajekt machine.
In a perfect world, Pages would face live pitching before returning to the Dodgers. But with not many arms available, Roberts indicated the team feels comfortable activating the 2026 All-Star without those additional reps.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Josue De Paula's Early Success Might Be Bad News For This Dodgers Veteran
item.dc:creator: Aaliyan Mohammed

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers called Josue De Paula up from Double-A earlier this month, and he has been making headlines with his bat early on.
It was the first time under Andrew Friedman that the Dodgers called a position player up directly from Double-A. De Paula's defense is not great, but Shohei Ohtani being injured has allowed him to serve as the designated hitter.
In 10 games, he is slashing .286/.474/.500 with half of his hits going for extra bases. His bat and eye at the plate have been as advertised. He is the Dodgers' top prospect and the No. 6 prospect in baseball. He won't be eligible for the postseason since he was not on the 40-man roster by Sept. 1, but his future for the Dodgers looks bright,
He is bound to slump at some point, but his early success means even if he is in Triple-A to start the season next year, it won't be long for him to be back with the big league club. However, Ohtani will be back, and De Paula will need a spot in the outfield. Unfortunately for Teoscar Hernández, he is the most likely to lose his job to De Paula.
Hernández has one year left on his contract, and his OPS has taken a big dive after his All-Star season in 2024. De Paula has shined with the bat and is working hard to improve his defense. If he can do that, he should take Hernández's spot.
What would that mean for Hernández? Well, it's not really the Dodgers' style to trade away their own stars, but De Paula needs to play. Hernández is about to be 34, and he still has trade value. He is not a great defender, so if De Paula is going to replace one of the Dodgers' starting outfielders, it's going to be the one who also isn't great defensively and is old. Kyle Tucker and Andy Pages are not going anywhere.
It's unclear what the Dodgers will do with De Paula next year. They've seen that his bat is ready for the big leagues, but may still want him to get some Triple-A work before making him an every day player in the big leagues. Eventually, he will start to slump in the Majors, like every young hitter, and will have to make adjustments. Regardless, his early success is a threat to Hernández's future with the team.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are gearing up for another potential deep playoff run.
LA clinched the NL West recently and is also looking to earn a first-round bye into the NLDS.
If you remember the Dodgers' 2025 World Series run, pitcher Roki Sasaki was a huge piece to the bullpen puzzle, as he slotted in as the team's closer in many big moments.
Well, Sasaki could be slated for a similar role this October.
More MLB on Heavy: Atlanta Braves Announce Pitcher News Before Reds Series
Roki Sasaki Set to Be Used in Bullpen Role Upon IL Activation
The Los Angeles Dodgers expect Roki Sasaki to be activated off the IL this week (Blister).
"The original plan was for Sasaki to go long as either a starter or a bulk guy, but now it looks like this might be more of a traditional relief outing to get him ready for coming out of the pen in October. It'll be Sasaki's first appearance since he went on the IL with a finger blister at the end of August."
In conjunction with Sasaki, Andy Pages is also likely to be activated on Tuesday.
The Dodgers bullpen group doesn't need nearly as much help this October as they did last year, but the bottom line regarding Sasaki is although he was a solid starter at times for LA this season, the Dodgers' playoff rotation is already locked in.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Get Major Andy Pages Update Ahead of Padres Series
Inside Roki Sasaki's 2026 Season Thus Far
Roki Sasaki endured his blister injury about a month ago in a start against the Atlanta Braves.
Before that development, Sasaki had made 23 starts, and he boasted a 4.60 ERA over 119.1 IP with 117 strikeouts.
Across 31 starts in his MLB career, Sasaki holds an ERA of 4.57 with 145 strikeouts in 155.2 total innings.
If Sasaki does happen to have a prominent role in the Dodgers' bullpen plans in October, it would be remarkable if he could recreate his magic from 2025.

item.title: [True Blue LA] Dodgers Week 26: Back in the postseason saddle again
item.dc:creator: Eric Stephen
item.description: The Dodgers are taking advantage of the schedule in front of them, with 14 wins in 19 September games, including winning the last 10 in a row at home.
